objects.description: Abstract base class for log4cxx Java-like objects, providing runtime class information and safe casting via a custom Class system. It declares virtual methods to obtain an object's Class, test instanceof, and perform casts. The DECLARE_LOG4CXX_CLAZZ_OBJECT(Object) macro adds static/registration helpers. LOG4CXX_PTR_DEF(Object) defines the shared-pointer alias ObjectPtr. A templated cast helper is also provided to cast between Object-derived types using the Class system.

Abstract metadata/registry class for log4cxx types. Provides a name (getName), a factory method (newInstance) returning a helpers::Object*, and static registry functions to look up (forName) and register (registerClass) classes by LogString. Copying is disabled; construction is protected for subclassing. The exact subclass list and ownership rules of returned Object instances are not specified here.
Base exception class for log4cxx helpers, carrying a fixed-size C-string message and overriding std::exception::what().
Represents exceptions thrown during normal operation; formats messages from status codes or explicit text.
Thrown when a null is used where an object/reference is required.
Indicates a method received an illegal or inappropriate argument.
Base class for I/O-related exceptions (failed or interrupted operations).
Thrown when a required resource (by key) is missing.
Indicates a failure related to an internal memory or resource pool; message derived from status code.
Signals a thread or operation was interrupted; optional status-based message.
Generic thread-related exception with status or message formatting.
Indicates a failure during character or data transcoding operations.
Thrown to indicate an object's monitor is used incorrectly (e.g., wait/notify without owning the monitor).
Thrown when attempting to instantiate an interface or abstract class.
Thrown when a class cannot be found by name during dynamic loading or reflection-like operations.
Indicates a requested element does not exist in the current context or collection.
Signals that a method has been invoked at an illegal or inappropriate time/state.
General socket-related I/O exception (e.g., TCP errors).
Thrown when a socket connection attempt is refused or otherwise fails to connect.
Indicates operations attempted on a closed socket/channel.
Thrown when binding a socket to a local address/port fails (e.g., port in use).
I/O operation was interrupted; indicates termination of transfer due to thread interruption.
Indicates a socket I/O operation timed out.

RAII-style wrapper around an APR memory pool (apr_pool_t) within the LOG4CXX_NS::helpers namespace. Provides creation and allocation helpers that allocate memory from the underlying APR pool, plus string duplication utilities. Holds an apr_pool_t* and a release flag controlling whether the destructor releases the APR pool. Copy construction/assignment are disabled. Exact destruction semantics are not fully specified in this header; consult implementation for whether ~Pool destroys the pool when release is true.

Singleton-style internal logging utility for log4cxx internals. Provides static methods to emit debug, warning, and error messages (optionally with exceptions), control quiet mode, and enable/disable debug and color output. Construction is private and managed via getInstance; instances are not intended to be user-created. The private implementation is hidden via a pimpl pointer (LogLogPrivate) declared through a macro here but not defined in this header.

objects.definition: typedef wchar_t logchar;
objects.description: Character type alias for the library’s configurable character type when LOG4CXX_LOGCHAR_IS_WCHAR is enabled. Typically a wide character element for strings.

objects.definition: typedef char logchar;
objects.description: Character type alias for the library’s configurable character type when LOG4CXX_LOGCHAR_IS_UTF8 is enabled. Represents UTF-8 code units when that mode is active.

objects.definition: typedef UniChar logchar;
objects.description: Character type alias for the library’s configurable character type when LOG4CXX_LOGCHAR_IS_UNICHAR is enabled. Uses 16-bit UniChar code units.

objects.definition: typedef std::basic_string<logchar> LogString;
objects.description: Primary string type used by log4cxx, bound to the configurable character type logchar. The actual character width/encoding depends on build-time macros (wchar_t, char for UTF-8, or UniChar).

Primary logging level class. Represents severity levels (OFF, FATAL, ERROR, WARN, INFO, DEBUG, TRACE, ALL), supports conversions from strings/integers, comparisons, and provides accessors to canonical singleton instances. Owns no external resources; instances are managed via shared pointers and factory methods. Construction is normally internal; users obtain shared instances via getX() or toLevel().
Meta-class helper for Level used by LOG4CXX runtime type and factory system. Provides name and conversion helpers used by macros. Typically not constructed directly by users.
Holds canonical shared instances of the standard logging levels. Accessed via Level::getData().

objects.description: Alias type for shared pointer to Level::Data. Used as return type for getData().

objects.definition: typedef std::shared_ptr<Level> LevelPtr;
objects.description: Shared pointer alias to Level used throughout the API for owning and passing Level instances.

Concrete log4cxx event object capturing all details of a single logging request (logger name, level, message, timestamp, thread info, location, MDC/NDC, and per-event properties). Instances are created with provided constructors and are non-copyable. Ownership of internal state is via a private implementation pointer.

LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEvent::LoggingEvent(const LogString& logger, const LevelPtr& level, const LogString& message, const LocationInfo& location)

objects.definition: LOG4CXX_LIST_DEF(KeySet, LogString);
objects.description: A list container typedef for holding a collection of LogString values used as key sets (e.g., MDC and property keys). The actual definition is generated by the LOG4CXX_LIST_DEF macro and is a list-like type within the spi namespace.

objects.definition: LOG4CXX_LIST_DEF(LoggingEventList, LoggingEventPtr);
objects.description: A list container typedef for collections of LoggingEventPtr elements. The underlying type is produced by the LOG4CXX_LIST_DEF macro.

Abstract base class for log4cxx appenders providing common functionality such as threshold filtering, filter chain management, layout handling, error handler support, and a synchronized doAppend that delegates to a subclass-implemented append(). It inherits from Appender and helpers::Object and is intended to be subclassed by concrete appenders.

Abstract interface for output targets (appenders) in log4cxx. Subclasses implement strategies to output logging events (e.g., to files, consoles, networks). Provides filter chaining, layout management, lifecycle close, and the core doAppend operation. Must be subclassed; not directly instantiable.

Abstract base class for Log4cxx layouts. It defines the interface for formatting LoggingEvent instances into textual output, optional header/footer emission, content type reporting, and whether the layout ignores embedded throwables. It inherits from spi::OptionHandler and helpers::Object. Construction is via subclasses only; destructor is virtual.

A concrete AppenderSkeleton-derived appender that writes logging events through a helpers::Writer (e.g., to an OutputStream) with configurable encoding and immediate flush behavior. It manages a Writer resource and header/footer emission via the layout. Construction variants include default, with layout and optional writer, and an internal private-impl constructor. Copy/assign are disabled.

A concrete appender that writes logging events to a file, optionally using buffered I/O with periodic flush via a background thread. Provides configuration for append mode, buffer size, buffered I/O enablement, and buffered flush interval. It derives from WriterAppender. Construction is via public constructors; file is actually opened on activateOptions. Destruction closes resources. Details of buffering thread behavior are managed internally and not exposed here.

Asynchronous appender that buffers LoggingEvent instances and forwards them to attached appenders on a background thread. Supports configurable ring-buffer size and blocking behavior when full. Implements spi::AppenderAttachable and AppenderSkeleton. Must be closed (typically via LogManager::shutdown) to flush and stop the dispatcher thread. Internal private struct AsyncAppenderPriv is declared but not defined here.

Forward-declared Appender interface/class for log4cxx appenders. Only a forward declaration is present in this header; the full definition is elsewhere. AppenderPtr is a std::shared_ptr alias to manage Appender instances.

Static-only utility class providing basic configuration helpers for log4cxx. It can attach a ConsoleAppender or a provided Appender (synchronous or asynchronous) to the root logger, optionally using a specified Layout. No instances are intended; constructor is protected and unused.

objects.definition: typedef std::shared_ptr<Appender> AppenderPtr;
objects.description: Type alias for a smart pointer managing LOG4CXX_NS::Appender instances via std::shared_ptr. Pointer form here is to the alias type itself, though typical usage passes AppenderPtr by value or const reference.

objects.definition:
namespace LOG4CXX_NS
{

/**
 *   Configures the repository from environmental settings and files.
*
*/
class LOG4CXX_EXPORT DefaultConfigurator
{
	private:
		DefaultConfigurator() {}

	public:
		/**
		Configure \c repository.

		If the configuration file name has not been provided by a call to setConfigurationFileName(),
		the environment variable "LOG4CXX_CONFIGURATION" or "log4j.configuration" value is used,
		with ${varname} instances using either a system environment variable value (if found)
		otherwise using the helpers::Properties object
		provided by spi::Configurator::properties.

		\usage
		~~~
		setenv LOG4CXX_CONFIGURATION="${PROGRAM_FILE_PATH.PARENT_PATH}/${PROGRAM_FILE_PATH.STEM}.xml"
		~~~

		Unless a custom configurator is specified using the
		"LOG4CXX_CONFIGURATOR_CLASS" or "log4j.configuratorClass"
		environment variable, the PropertyConfigurator will be used to
		configure log4cxx unless the file name ends with the ".xml"
		extension, in which case the DOMConfigurator will be used. If a
		custom configurator is specified, the environment variable should
		contain a fully qualified class name of a class that implements the
		Configurator interface.

		If the configuration file name is not found using any of the previous approaches,
		the current directory is examined for a file with extension ".xml" or ".properties"
		with a base name "log4cxx" or "log4j".

		If a positive number has been provided by a call to setConfigurationWatchSeconds()
		or the environment variables "LOG4CXX_CONFIGURATION_WATCH_SECONDS" contains a positive number
		a background thread is started that will periodically check for a change to the configuration file
		and apply any configuration changes found.

		Call the spi::LoggerRepository::isConfigured \c repository member function
		to determine whether a configuration file was found.
		*/
		static void configure(spi::LoggerRepositoryPtr repository);

		/**
		Attempt configuration by calling configure() passing the default repository.

		See configure() for how the configuration file name is determined.

		@return a success indicator.
		*/
		static spi::ConfigurationStatus tryConfigure();

		/**
		Make \c path the configuration file used by configure().

		Any ${varname} instances in the \c path value are expanded
		using either a system environment variable value (if found)
		otherwise using the map provided by spi::Configurator::properties.

		\usage
		~~~{.cpp}
		DefaultConfigurator::setConfigurationFileName(LOG4CXX_STR("${PROGRAM_FILE_PATH.PARENT_PATH}/${PROGRAM_FILE_PATH.STEM}.xml"))
		~~~

		*/
		static void setConfigurationFileName(const LogString& path);

		/**
		Make \c seconds the time a background thread will delay before checking
		for a change to the configuration file used by configure().

		\usage
		~~~{.cpp}
		DefaultConfigurator::setConfigurationWatchSeconds(1);
		~~~
		*/
		static void setConfigurationWatchSeconds(int seconds);

		/**
		 * Call configure() passing the default repository
		 * after calling setConfigurationFileName() with a path composed of
		 * an entry in \c directories and an entry in \c filenames
		 * when the combination identifies an existing file.
		 *
		 \usage
		 ~~~{.cpp}
		 std::vector<LogString> directories
		     { LOG4CXX_STR(".")
		     , LOG4CXX_STR("${PROGRAM_FILE_PATH.PARENT_PATH}")
		     };
		 std::vector<LogString> filenames
		     { LOG4CXX_STR("${PROGRAM_FILE_PATH.STEM}.xml")
		     , LOG4CXX_STR("${PROGRAM_FILE_PATH.STEM}.properties")
		     , LOG4CXX_STR("log4cxx.xml")
		     };
		 DefaultConfigurator::configureFromFile(directories, filenames);
		 ~~~
		 *
		 * Using the above example and an executable file named "myapp"
		 * installed in the  directory "/opt/com.foo/bin",
		 * locations are checked in the following order:
		 * -# "./myapp.xml"
		 * -# "./myapp.properties"
		 * -# "./log4cxx.xml"
		 * -# "/opt/com.foo/bin/myapp.xml"
		 * -# "/opt/com.foo/bin/myapp.properties"
		 * -# "/opt/com.foo/bin/log4cxx.xml"
		 *
		 * If a file exists but it is not able to be used to configure Log4cxx,
		 * the next file in the combinatorial set will be tried until
		 * a valid configuration file is found or
		 * all values in the combinatorial set have been tried.
		 *
		 * @param directories The directories to look in.
		 * @param filenames The names of the files to look for
		 * @return a success indicator and the configuration file path that was used (if found).
		 */
		static std::tuple<spi::ConfigurationStatus,LogString> configureFromFile
			( const std::vector<LogString>& directories
			, const std::vector<LogString>& filenames
			);

	private:
		static const LogString getConfigurationFileName();
		static const LogString getConfiguratorClass();
		static int getConfigurationWatchDelay();

};	 // class DefaultConfigurator
}  // namespace log4cxx
objects.description: A utility class offering static helpers to configure a log4cxx LoggerRepository from environment variables and configuration files. It is non-instantiable (private default constructor) and provides methods to set configuration file name, watch interval, perform configuration, and attempt configuration from candidate directories/filenames. Details about internal behavior beyond declarations are not present in this header.

Forward declaration of the Logger class in the LOG4CXX_NS namespace. Only a declaration is present in this header; the class definition appears elsewhere. LoggerPtr is a typedef alias to std::shared_ptr<Logger>.
Typedef alias within LOG4CXX_NS: LoggerPtr is an alias for std::shared_ptr<Logger>. It is used as the return type of makeNewLoggerInstance.

Concrete factory (available when LOG4CXX_ABI_VERSION <= 15) implementing spi::LoggerFactory and helpers::Object. Provides makeNewLoggerInstance to create Logger objects by name. The method is marked deprecated because Pool is no longer required. Lifetime is typically managed via base interfaces; no destructor is declared here. Construction is default; no custom constructors are defined in this header.

Concrete Layout subclass that formats logging events into an HTML table. Provides options for including source location information and setting a document title. Exposes typical Layout overrides for content type, header/footer, formatting, and throwable handling. Uses a private implementation pointer declared via LOG4CXX_DECLARE_PRIVATE_MEMBER_PTR. Destructor is non-virtual in this header but class derives from Layout which should have a virtual destructor; assume safe polymorphic deletion through Layout*.

A Layout-derived class that renders logging events as JSON dictionaries. Supports options for including location info, thread identifiers, and pretty-printed output. Provides formatting via format() and content type reporting as application/json. Construction and lifetime are managed by users or shared pointer aliases provided by LOG4CXX_PTR_DEF.

Concrete Layout that renders a LoggingEvent as: "<LEVEL> - <message>\n". It ignores any throwable/exception information (ignoresThrowable returns true) and has no configurable options (activateOptions and setOption are no-ops). Inherits from Layout and participates in log4cxx runtime type/cast system via DECLARE_LOG4CXX_OBJECT and CAST_MAP macros.

Forward-declared logger class in the LOG4CXX_NS namespace. Only an incomplete declaration is present in this header; its full definition is elsewhere. LoggerPtr is defined as std::shared_ptr<Logger> and is used within ProvisionNode. Details about construction and lifecycle are unknown in this file.

objects.definition: typedef std::shared_ptr<Logger> LoggerPtr;
objects.description: Alias for std::shared_ptr<LOG4CXX_NS::Logger>. Represents a shared-ownership smart pointer to a Logger. Construction and deletion follow std::shared_ptr semantics.

objects.definition: typedef std::vector<LoggerPtr> ProvisionNode;
objects.description: Alias for std::vector<LOG4CXX_NS::LoggerPtr>. Represents a collection of log4cxx Logger shared pointers used during provisioning/initialization of the logger hierarchy. Standard std::vector semantics apply.

Concrete logger repository for log4cxx that manages the logger hierarchy, thresholds, configuration state, and repository-wide events. It provides creation and retrieval of Logger instances, root logger access, threshold control, configuration lifecycle (ensureIsConfigured, reset, shutdown), and listener management. Construction is via the static create() factory; the default constructor is private. Copying is disabled. Internal state is pimpl-ed via HierarchyPrivate (definition not present here).

RAII smart-pointer-like helper that manages a LoggerPtr retrieved from LogManager and conditionally removes the underlying Logger from the repository on destruction/reset if it did not previously exist in configuration and is not otherwise referenced. Provides implicit conversions to LoggerPtr, pointer-like access, and reset methods (default and named) to manage lifecycle. Details about LoggerPtr and LogManager are external to this header.

Forward declaration of Logger class used throughout log4cxx. The header defines aliases: LoggerPtr as a shared_ptr to Logger and LoggerList as a std::vector of LoggerPtr. The actual Logger class definition is not present here.
Forward declaration of LoggerFactory used to create Logger instances. A shared_ptr alias LoggerFactoryPtr is provided. The actual class definition is not present here.

Facade/manager class for obtaining and managing Logger instances and the active LoggerRepository. All methods are static; the class maintains an internal guard and a RepositorySelector to route repository access. Construction is not exposed; it is used via its static API.

Abstract base class for lightweight logging streams that emulate std::basic_ostream formatting without unnecessary overhead. Holds a logger, a level, and a location, and provides formatting state manipulation. Derived classes implement buffering and dispatch via log().
Concrete logging stream using char as character type. Buffers into an internal std::basic_stringstream<char> and dispatches on end-of-message. Not thread-safe; intended for short-lived use.
Concrete logging stream using wchar_t as character type. Available when LOG4CXX_WCHAR_T_API is enabled. Not thread-safe; short-lived usage recommended.

objects.definition: typedef logstream_base& (*logstream_manipulator)(logstream_base&);
objects.description: Function pointer typedef for manipulators compatible with logstream_base (e.g., endmsg, nop). Pointer form is a pointer to this function-pointer type.

RAII helper and static manager for per-thread Nested Diagnostic Contexts (NDC) in log4cxx. Constructing an NDC with a message pushes it on the current thread’s context stack; destruction pops it. Provides static APIs to push/peek/pop messages, query emptiness/depth, clear/remove all for the thread, clone the current thread’s stack for inheritance into child threads, and inherit a provided stack. Thread-local behavior is implied; memory ownership notes: cloneStack returns a heap-allocated Stack* that callers must delete unless passed to inherit, which deletes the provided pointer during the call.

objects.definition: typedef std::pair<LogString, LogString> DiagnosticContext;
objects.description: Alias within NDC representing a single context entry as a pair of strings: message and the accumulated full message. Both elements are LogString.

objects.definition: typedef std::stack<DiagnosticContext> Stack;
objects.description: Alias within NDC representing the per-thread stack of DiagnosticContext entries. Used for cloning and inheritance between threads.

class LOG4CXX_EXPORT MDC { public: /** String to string stl map. */ typedef std::map Map; /** * Places a key/value pair in the MDC for the current thread * which will be removed during the corresponding destructor. Both * construction and destruction are expected to be on the same thread. * @param key context identifier * @param value a string that distinguishes this context. */ MDC(const std::string& key, const std::string& value); ~MDC(); /** * Set the key context in the current thread's context map to value. * *

If the current thread does not have a context map it is * created as a side effect. * @param key context identifier * @param value a string that distinguishes this context. */ static void put(const std::string& key, const std::string& value); /** * Set the key context in the current thread's context map to value. * *

If the current thread does not have a context map it is * created as a side effect. * */ static void putLS(const LogString& key, const LogString& value); /** * Get the context identified by the key parameter. * *

This method has no side effects. * @param key context identifier. * @return value for key, empty if not set. * */ static std::string get(const std::string& key); /** * Gets the context identified by the key parameter. * @param key context key. * @param dest destination to which value is appended. * @return true if key has associated value. */ static bool get(const LogString& key, LogString& dest); /** * Remove the the context identified by the key * parameter. * @param key context identifier. * @return value if key had been set, empty if not. */ static std::string remove(const std::string& key); #if LOG4CXX_WCHAR_T_API /** * Places a key/value pair in the MDC for the current thread * which will be removed during the corresponding destructor. Both * construction and destruction are expected to be on the same thread. * @param key context identifier * @param value a string that distinguishes this context. */ MDC(const std::wstring& key, const std::wstring& value); /** * Set the key context in the current thread's context map to value. * *

If the current thread does not have a context map it is * created as a side effect. * @param key context identifier * @param value a string that distinguishes this context. */ static void put(const std::wstring& key, const std::wstring& value); /** * Get the context identified by the key parameter. * *

This method has no side effects. * @param key context identifier. * @return value for key, empty if not set. * */ static std::wstring get(const std::wstring& key); /** * Remove the the context identified by the key * parameter. * @param key context identifier. * @return value if key had been set, empty if not. */ static std::wstring remove(const std::wstring& key); #endif #if LOG4CXX_UNICHAR_API /** * Places a key/value pair in the MDC for the current thread * which will be removed during the corresponding destructor. Both * construction and destruction are expected to be on the same thread. * @param key context identifier * @param value a string that distinguishes this context. */ MDC(const std::basic_string& key, const std::basic_string& value); /** * Set the key context in the current thread's context map to value. * *

If the current thread does not have a context map it is * created as a side effect. * @param key context identifier * @param value the value. */ static void put(const std::basic_string& key, const std::basic_string& value); /** * Get the context identified by the key parameter. * *

This method has no side effects. * @param key context identifier. * @return value for key, empty if not set. * */ static std::basic_string get(const std::basic_string& key); /** * Remove the the context identified by the key * parameter. * @param key context identifier. * @return value if key had been set, empty if not. */ static std::basic_string remove(const std::basic_string& key); #endif #if LOG4CXX_CFSTRING_API /** * Places a key/value pair in the MDC for the current thread * which will be removed during the corresponding destructor. Both * construction and destruction are expected to be on the same thread. * @param key context identifier * @param value a string that distinguishes this context. */ MDC(const CFStringRef& key, const CFStringRef& value); /** * Set the key context in the current thread's context map to value. * *

If the current thread does not have a context map it is * created as a side effect. * @param key context identifier * @param value a string that distinguishes this context. */ static void put(const CFStringRef& key, const CFStringRef& value); /** * Get the context identified by the key parameter. * *

This method has no side effects. * @param key context identifier. * @return value for key, empty if not set. * */ static CFStringRef get(const CFStringRef& key); /** * Remove the the context identified by the key * parameter. * @param key context identifier. * @return value if key had been set, empty if not. */ static CFStringRef remove(const CFStringRef& key); #endif /** * Remove the the context identified by the key * parameter. * @param key context identifier. * @param prevValue buffer to which previous value is appended. * @return true if key existed in MDC. */ static bool remove(const LogString& key, LogString& prevValue); /** * Clear all entries in the MDC. *

A thread that adds to the diagnostic context by calling * #put should call this method before exiting * to prevent unbounded memory usage. */ static void clear(); private: MDC(const MDC&); MDC& operator=(const MDC&); LOG4CXX_DECLARE_PRIVATE_MEMBER(LogString, key) };
objects.description: Mapped Diagnostic Context class. Provides per-thread map of key/value pairs to tag log events. RAII constructor records a key/value on creation and removes it on destruction in the same thread. Includes static APIs to put/get/remove keys (multiple overloads for different string types) and clear the thread-local map. Copying is disabled. Details of storage and lifetime are internal to log4cxx. Unknowns: exact thread-local mechanism and memory ownership are not visible here.

Main configurator class for log4cxx property files. Provides APIs to configure logging from a properties file or Properties object, optionally watch files for changes, and parse/attach appenders and loggers. In newer ABI versions, uses an internal PrivateData pimpl. Construction is default; destruction should be via standard delete or smart pointers as managed by the framework. Threading: configureAndWatch spawns a watchdog thread stopped by LogManager::shutdown.

DOM-based XML configurator for Log4cxx. Provides APIs to parse XML configuration files/elements and configure appenders, loggers, layouts, filters, policies, and levels. Inherits from spi::Configurator and offers multiple static configure/configureAndWatch helpers and an instance doConfigure. Non-copyable; uses a private implementation pointer (DOMConfiguratorPrivate).
Opaque forward declaration of APR XML document structure used when parsing XML. Only referenced; no fields are defined here.
Opaque forward declaration of APR XML element structure used when parsing XML. Only referenced; no fields are defined here.

Concrete layout that formats LoggingEvent instances as log4j XML (log4j:event) fragments. It derives from Layout and supports options for including source location information and MDC properties. Exceptions are included (ignoresThrowable returns false). Private data is managed via an internal pimpl pointer declared through a macro; details are not exposed here.

Appender that buffers recent logging events and sends them via SMTP when a TriggeringEventEvaluator deems an event should trigger an email. Manages SMTP server details, recipients, subject, credentials, buffer size, and evaluator configuration. Requires a Layout. Lifetime managed by typical log4cxx appender ownership; copy/assignment disabled; uses a private pimpl struct SMTPPriv (incomplete here).

Abstract base class for network socket-based appenders (e.g., SocketAppender, XMLSocketAppender). Manages remote host/port configuration, optional location info, reconnection delay, and connection lifecycle. Provides abstract hooks for derived classes to set the active socket, perform cleanup, and supply default delay/port. This header declares the interface only; implementation details are not present here.

Appender that sends log events to a remote syslog daemon. Provides configuration for syslog host, facility, and maximum message length, and splits oversized messages for RFC 3164 compatibility. Requires a Layout. Note: actual member fields and the SyslogAppenderPriv definition are not present in this header; they are likely defined in the corresponding source file using the PIMPL pattern.
direct_api_constructors: SyslogAppender(const LayoutPtr& layout, const LogString& syslogHost, int syslogFacility)

objects.description: Appender that listens on a TCP port and streams logging events to connected clients (e.g., via telnet). It derives from AppenderSkeleton. Exposes configuration for port, hostname, max connections, encoding, and SO_REUSEADDR. Internally uses a hidden pimpl struct TelnetAppenderPriv for implementation details. Actual constructor/destructor behavior and resource ownership are not visible in this header; details such as thread and socket management are handled internally.

Appender that sends LoggingEvent records over TCP to a remote log server, typically serialized as XML (but can be used with other layouts, e.g., JSON). Inherits from SocketAppenderSkeleton. Provides defaults for port and reconnection delay, manages socket setup/cleanup, and implements append to transmit events. Not copyable. Contains an internal opaque private struct forward-declared here.

Appender that logs events to a database using APR database support. It is a concrete AppenderSkeleton subclass configurable with driver name/params, database name, an SQL statement, and column mappings. Does not require a layout. Provides lifecycle methods (activateOptions, append, close) and SQL setter/getter. Construction is default; copy is disabled. Note: internal implementation is hidden via the protected nested struct DBAppenderPriv (pimpl).

Custom exception type for ODBC-related failures in the db namespace. It can be constructed from ODBC handle information or a message, and formats a diagnostic message using the provided ODBC handle and pool. Copy-constructible. No destructor explicitly declared; relies on base Exception. Specific error fields and lifetime details of returned message are not documented here.

Appender that writes LoggingEvent data to a database via ODBC using a configurable SQL INSERT statement and column mappings. Buffers events up to a configurable size before executing batched inserts. Exposes overridable connection management hooks (getConnection/closeConnection) for pooling. Provides options to set DSN/URL/ConnectionString, User, Password, BufferSize, SQL, and column mapping. Threading, lifetime, and error handling rely on AppenderSkeleton semantics; errors may throw SQLException or be reported to the error handler. Includes utility encode helpers for wide char conversions and a private pImpl struct ODBCAppenderPriv (defined elsewhere).

objects.definition: typedef void* SQLHDBC;
objects.description: Type alias within ODBCAppender for an ODBC database connection handle; represented as a void* in this header. Used by getConnection/closeConnection.

objects.definition: typedef void* SQLHENV;
objects.description: Type alias within ODBCAppender for an ODBC environment handle; represented as a void* in this header. Not otherwise used in publicly visible methods here.

objects.definition: typedef void* SQLHANDLE;
objects.description: Generic ODBC handle alias scoped to ODBCAppender; void* here. Present for completeness; not used by public methods in this header.

objects.definition: typedef short SQLSMALLINT;
objects.description: Small integer alias for ODBC types within ODBCAppender. Provided for compatibility with ODBC signatures used internally.

A log4cxx appender that writes to a file and performs rollovers according to configured RollingPolicy and TriggeringPolicy. Provides APIs to configure max backup index, max file size, date-based patterns, and to query/adjust current file length. Owns internal private implementation via RollingFileAppenderPriv. Construction typically via default constructor; lifetime managed like other appenders. Details about destruction are inherited from FileAppender.

Subclass of RollingFileAppender that coordinates log file rolling across multiple processes. Adds synchronization logic to safely detect and perform rollovers, reopen files after rotation, and manage current file sizes. Suitable when multiple processes write to the same rolling log file. Overhead is higher than RollingFileAppender. Details of synchronization are implemented privately.

Abstract interface for log4cxx rolling policies. It defines the contract for initializing and performing log file rollovers and provides the active log file used by rolling appenders. Implementations must derive from this class and OptionHandler, and implement initialize and rollover. Destruction and lifetime are managed by smart pointer alias RollingPolicyPtr. Details of construction are via factory or configuration, not visible here.

Abstract base class for rolling policies in Log4cxx. Provides common option handling, file name pattern storage/parsing, and helpers to format output file names using date/index pattern converters. Inherits RollingPolicy and helpers::Object; also implements spi::OptionHandler via cast map. Construction/destruction are provided; one protected ctor accepts a private-impl pointer. Details of the private data (RollingPolicyBasePrivate) are hidden by macros and not defined here.

Concrete rolling policy that performs time-based rollover of log files. It derives from RollingPolicyBase and TriggeringPolicy, supports date-patterned file names, optional compression (.gz/.zip), and decoupling active and archived file locations. It also contains multiprocess support via shared-memory/mmap bookkeeping for the last file name. Construction is via default constructor; configure FileNamePattern (and optionally ActiveFileName) before use, then call activateOptions prior to appender activation. Destruction is virtual; private implementation is hidden with a pimpl pointer. Details about the private type TimeBasedRollingPolicyPrivate are not present in this header.

A rolling policy trigger that initiates a rollover when the active log file size reaches or exceeds a configured maximum. Inherits TriggeringPolicy. Holds a maxFileSize value and exposes getters/setters, option handling, and a predicate isTriggeringEvent used by rolling appenders. Construction is via default constructor; no special destruction noted. Details of TriggeringPolicy and related types are external to this header.

Concrete rolling policy implementing a fixed-window rename strategy for log files. On rollover it shifts archived files within a bounded index window and renames the active log to the minimum index, deleting the oldest if needed. Window size is effectively capped at 12 via MAX_WINDOW_SIZE. Requires ActiveFileName and a FileNamePattern containing an integer token (%i). Unknown internal details are encapsulated via the private pimpl struct.

A rolling policy component that triggers log rollover based on a chain of filters. It evaluates each logging event against the filter list and signals rollover unless a filter rejects the event. Implements TriggeringPolicy and integrates with OptionHandler for configuration. Details of private storage are hidden via a pimpl pointer.

Abstract base class in LOG4CXX_NS::rolling that decides when a rolling appender should trigger a rollover (e.g., based on time, size, or custom logic). It inherits from spi::OptionHandler and helpers::Object and declares a pure virtual method isTriggeringEvent that implementations must provide. The LOG4CXX_PTR_DEF macro declares a smart pointer alias TriggeringPolicyPtr for this type.

Concrete log4cxx filter that unconditionally denies all logging events. Useful as a terminal filter to switch a chain into a “deny by default” mode. Inherits from spi::Filter and overrides decide() to always return DENY. Construction/destruction follow standard C++ semantics; no extra ownership rules are specified here.

Concrete log4cxx filter that matches logging events based on an exact Level. It inherits from spi::Filter and supports options to set a level string and whether to accept or deny on match. Internals are hidden via a private pImpl struct LevelMatchFilterPrivate (definition not present here).

objects.definition: class Level;
objects.description: Forward declaration of LOG4CXX_NS::Level. Only declared here; the full definition is in another header. Included due to this filter operating on log levels.

A log4cxx filter that accepts or rejects logging events based on whether their level lies within an inclusive [levelMin, levelMax] range. Behavior on match is controlled by acceptOnMatch (ACCEPT if true, NEUTRAL if false). If levelMin is unset there is no minimum; if levelMax is unset there is no maximum. Inherits spi::Filter. Destructor and behavior details beyond the interface are not shown here.

Filter subclass that conditionally accepts or denies logging events based on source location information (method name and/or line number). Supports configuration via setOption for Method, LineNumber, Operator (And/Or), and AcceptOnMatch. Internally uses a private implementation struct (LocationInfoFilterPrivate). Construction/destruction are default; usage is to instantiate, configure, and use within Log4cxx filtering chain.

A log4cxx filter that matches logging events by the logger name. If the event's logger name matches the configured loggerToMatch, the decision is ACCEPT or DENY depending on acceptOnMatch; otherwise NEUTRAL. Inherits from spi::Filter. Supports options LoggerToMatch and AcceptOnMatch via setOption. Actual storage is likely hidden in a private implementation struct (pimpl).

A log4cxx filter that performs simple string matching on a LoggingEvent’s message. If the configured StringToMatch is found in the message, the filter will either ACCEPT or DENY based on AcceptOnMatch; otherwise it returns NEUTRAL. It derives from spi::Filter and participates in the log4cxx RTTI/cast system. Uses a private implementation (StringMatchFilterPrivate) via an incomplete struct declaration. The LOG4CXX_PTR_DEF macro declares a smart/shared pointer alias StringMatchFilterPtr.

A concrete log4cxx filter that performs a logical AND over a chain of contained filters. All contained filters must return Filter::ACCEPT for this filter to consider it a match; otherwise it returns Filter::NEUTRAL. The final decision is governed by the acceptOnMatch setting: on match, return ACCEPT if true, otherwise DENY. It derives from LOG4CXX_NS::spi::Filter, is non-copyable, and likely maintains internal state via a private implementation struct AndFilterPrivate. Methods: addFilter to append a child filter; setAcceptOnMatch to control decision on match; decide implements filtering for a LoggingEvent. Construction/destruction are via default ctor/dtor. Details of storage and ownership of child filters are not present here and are managed internally.

A log4cxx filter that evaluates the current thread's MDC (mapped diagnostic context) against configured key/value pairs. It supports matching either all pairs (AND) or any pair (OR) and can be configured to accept or deny on match. It derives from LOG4CXX_NS::spi::Filter and integrates with log4cxx's object/cast system. Internals are hidden via an incomplete private struct (pimpl) declared but not defined here.

A log4cxx Filter implementation that augments each processed LoggingEvent by adding properties parsed from a configured comma-separated list of key=value pairs. It does not overwrite existing event properties. Holds an internal PropertyMap (std::map<LogString,LogString>) pointer for configured properties. Copy construction/assignment are declared private (unimplemented) to prevent copying.

Concrete log4cxx Layout that formats logging events using the {fmt} library style placeholders (e.g., {level}, {message}). Accepts a ConversionPattern string and implements format(), ignoresThrowable(), activateOptions(), and setOption(). Internally uses a private implementation (FMTLayoutPrivate) via a declared private pointer. Construction can be default or with a pattern string.

Strongly-typed enum of bit flags controlling hexdump output formatting within LOG4CXX_NS. Values include None, AddStartingNewline, AddEndingNewline, and the combined AddNewline. Bitwise helpers (& as test, | as combine) are defined inline for convenience.

ErrorHandler implementation that switches logging to a backup appender if the primary appender fails. It integrates with log4cxx's object/cast system and tracks involved loggers. Construction/destruction follow normal C++ semantics; ownership of appenders and loggers is managed via smart pointer types (AppenderPtr, LoggerPtr). Behavior details of failure detection/transfer are implemented in the source file; this header declares the interface.

functions.name: log4cxx::libraryVersion
functions.description: Returns the compiled log4cxx library version as a 32-bit integer. The value is packed using LOG4CXX_MAKE_VERSION(major, minor, patch, tweak) and can be unpacked with LOG4CXX_VERSION_GET_MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH/TWEAK macros. Typical usage is to call this at runtime to verify or log the version in use and, if needed, compare it to the compile-time LOG4CXX_VERSION. Thread-safety and side effects are not documented.
requirements: No arguments are required.
No specific caller state or initialization is documented.
Interpret the returned 32-bit value using the LOG4CXX_VERSION_GET_* macros if you need individual components (major/minor/patch/tweak).

functions.signature:
template<typename Ret, typename Type, bool = std::is_base_of<Ret, LOG4CXX_NS::helpers::Object>::value, bool = std::is_base_of<Type, LOG4CXX_NS::helpers::Object>::value>

functions.description: Template helper that attempts to cast a shared_ptr<Type> to shared_ptr<Ret> using log4cxx’s Class-based runtime casting. functions.description: Unconditionally emits the given message to SystemErrWriter, unless quiet mode is enabled (quiet mode suppresses all output, including errors). Intended for reporting internal errors.

Output is suppressed if quiet mode is enabled (see setQuietMode).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::helpers::LogLog::setQuietMode
functions.description: Enables or disables quiet mode. In quiet mode LogLog generates no output at all, not even for errors.
requirements: Parameter newValue sets quiet mode (true = no output, false = allow output).
Callable at any time; global effect on all LogLog output.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::helpers::LogLog::warn
functions.description: Unconditionally emits the given message to SystemErrWriter as a warning, unless quiet mode is enabled.
requirements: msg may be any LogString; must be a valid reference.
Output is suppressed if quiet mode is enabled (see setQuietMode).

functions.name: LOGLOG_DEBUG
functions.description: Convenience macro that conditionally emits an internal log4cxx debug message. Expands to: if (LogLog::isDebugEnabled()) LOG4CXX_NS::helpers::LogLog::debug(log); Use to report log4cxx internal diagnostics that should appear only when internal debugging is enabled. Output is suppressed when internal debugging is disabled or when LogLog quiet mode is active.
requirements: Include this header and ensure LOG4CXX_NS resolves to the correct namespace for log4cxx before use.
Argument 'log' must be a LOG4CXX_NS::LogString or an expression implicitly convertible to const LOG4CXX_NS::LogString&.
Caller must not rely on evaluation of 'log' when internal debug logging is disabled; the expression may not be evaluated at all in that case.
Usable only where a statement is valid (macro expands to a compound statement).

functions.name: LOGLOG_WARN
functions.description: Convenience macro that unconditionally emits an internal log4cxx warning message. Expands to: LOG4CXX_NS::helpers::LogLog::warn(log); Intended for reporting noteworthy internal conditions. Output may still be suppressed if LogLog quiet mode is enabled.
requirements: Include this header and ensure LOG4CXX_NS resolves to the correct namespace for log4cxx before use.
Argument 'log' must be a LOG4CXX_NS::LogString or an expression implicitly convertible to const LOG4CXX_NS::LogString&.
Usable only where a statement is valid (macro expands to a compound statement).

functions.name: LOGLOG_ERROR
functions.description: Convenience macro that, per this header’s definition, forwards to LogLog::warn(log) rather than LogLog::error(log). Expands to: LOG4CXX_NS::helpers::LogLog::warn(log); This likely produces a warn-level internal message instead of error-level. Treat as warning unless this is intentional in your version. Output may be suppressed if LogLog quiet mode is enabled.
requirements: Include this header and ensure LOG4CXX_NS resolves to the correct namespace for log4cxx before use.
Argument 'log' must be a LOG4CXX_NS::LogString or an expression implicitly convertible to const LOG4CXX_NS::LogString&.
Usable only where a statement is valid (macro expands to a compound statement).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Level::Level
functions.signature: LOG4CXX_NS::Level::Level(int level, const LOG4CXX_NS::LogString& name, int syslogEquivalent)
functions.description: Constructs a Level object with a numeric severity, a display name, and a syslog-equivalent integer. Typically used internally to create predefined levels (OFF, FATAL, ERROR, WARN, INFO, DEBUG, TRACE, ALL).
requirements: level is an integer representing severity ordering (higher means more severe based on the enum constants in this header).
name is the textual name of the level; it should be a valid LogString.
syslogEquivalent is the integer code corresponding to syslog severity for this level.
Copy and assignment are disabled for Level (private copy ctor/assignment).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Level::toLevel
functions.description: Parses a narrow string level name and returns the corresponding Level instance. If parsing fails, returns the DEBUG level.
requirements: sArg should be a recognized level name (e.g., "OFF", "FATAL", "ERROR", "WARN", "INFO", "DEBUG", "TRACE", "ALL").
Returned pointer refers to a shared singleton Level instance.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Level::toLevel
functions.signature: static LOG4CXX_NS::LevelPtr LOG4CXX_NS::Level::toLevel(const std::string& sArg, const LOG4CXX_NS::LevelPtr& defaultLevel)
functions.description: Parses a narrow string level name and returns the corresponding Level instance. If parsing fails, returns the provided defaultLevel.
requirements: sArg should be a recognized level name to avoid falling back to default.
defaultLevel should be a valid LevelPtr when a fallback is desired; behavior is unspecified if it is null.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Level::toString
functions.description: Appends this level’s name to the provided std::string buffer using the current encoding.
requirements: name must be a valid std::string instance; the method appends to the buffer rather than clearing it.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Level::toLevelLS
functions.description: Parses a LogString level name and returns the corresponding Level instance. If parsing fails, returns the DEBUG level.
requirements: sArg should be a recognized level name (e.g., OFF, FATAL, ERROR, WARN, INFO, DEBUG, TRACE, ALL) in the library’s LogString encoding.
Returned pointer refers to a shared singleton Level instance.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Level::getData
functions.description: Returns a shared structure containing the singleton Level instances for standard levels (Off, Fatal, Error, Warn, Info, Debug, Trace, All).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Level::getAll
functions.description: Returns the singleton Level instance representing ALL (least severe).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Level::getFatal
functions.description: Returns the singleton Level instance representing FATAL.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Level::getError
functions.description: Returns the singleton Level instance representing ERROR.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Level::getWarn
functions.description: Returns the singleton Level instance representing WARN.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Level::getInfo
functions.description: Returns the singleton Level instance representing INFO.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Level::getDebug
functions.description: Returns the singleton Level instance representing DEBUG.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Level::getTrace
functions.description: Returns the singleton Level instance representing TRACE.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Level::getOff
functions.description: Returns the singleton Level instance representing OFF (most severe, disables logging).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Level::equals
functions.signature: virtual bool LOG4CXX_NS::Level::equals(const LOG4CXX_NS::LevelPtr& level) const
functions.description: Compares this Level to another for equality based on their numeric severity values.
requirements: level should reference a valid Level instance; behavior is unspecified if null.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Level::isGreaterOrEqual
functions.signature: virtual bool LOG4CXX_NS::Level::isGreaterOrEqual(const LOG4CXX_NS::LevelPtr& level) const
functions.description: Returns true if this Level’s severity is greater than or equal to the provided level’s severity; false otherwise.
requirements: level should reference a valid Level instance; behavior is unspecified if null.
Intended to be used without overriding in typical usage, per documentation note.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Level::getSyslogEquivalent
functions.description: Returns the syslog-equivalent severity code for this Level.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Level::toInt
functions.description: Returns the numeric severity value of this Level.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Level::LevelClass::getName
functions.description: Returns the runtime class name string for Level ("Level").

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Level::LevelClass::toLevel
functions.description: Converts a LogString to a Level by delegating to Level::toLevelLS.
requirements: sArg should be a recognized level name for deterministic results.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEvent::LoggingEvent
functions.description: Default constructor. Creates an empty logging event with no logger, level, message, or location set. Typically populated later by the logging framework before use.
requirements: Object must not be copied or assigned (copy constructor and assignment operator are declared private).
No additional requirements stated.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEvent::~LoggingEvent
functions.description: Destructor for LoggingEvent. Releases any resources held by the event. Typically invoked automatically when the event goes out of scope or its smart pointer reference count reaches zero.
requirements: No explicit requirements stated; ensure the object is not used after destruction.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEvent::getLevel
functions.description: Returns the severity level associated with this logging event.
requirements: This method does not modify the object and may be called at any time after construction.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEvent::getLoggerName
functions.description: Returns the name of the logger that produced this event.
requirements: This method does not modify the object and may be called at any time after construction.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEvent::getMessage
functions.description: Returns the original message provided for this event (prior to any renderer processing).
requirements: This method does not modify the object and may be called at any time after construction.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEvent::getRenderedMessage
functions.description: Returns the message for this event, potentially after renderer processing. Use renderMessage() to force rendering if needed.
requirements: This method does not modify the object.
If the caller requires renderer-produced output, call renderMessage() beforehand.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEvent::getStartTime
functions.description: Returns the number of microseconds since the Unix epoch at the time the application started (process start reference).
requirements: Static function; may be called without an instance.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEvent::getThreadName
functions.description: Returns the identity of the thread in which this event was created.
requirements: This method does not modify the object and may be called at any time after construction.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEvent::getThreadUserName
functions.description: Returns the user-assigned name of the thread that created this event (if available). Falls back to the thread identity if a platform-specific name could not be retrieved.
requirements: This method does not modify the object and may be called at any time after construction.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEvent::getTimeStamp
functions.description: Returns the number of microseconds since 1970-01-01 at the time this logging event was created.
requirements: This method does not modify the object and may be called at any time after construction.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEvent::getChronoTimeStamp
functions.description: Returns the std::chrono system_clock time_point captured when this event was created.
requirements: This method does not modify the object and may be called at any time after construction.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEvent::getLocationInformation
functions.description: Returns the source code location where the logging request was made.
requirements: This method does not modify the object and may be called at any time after construction.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEvent::getNDC
functions.description: Appends the current nested diagnostic context (NDC) for this event to dest. Returns true if dest was modified. To obtain correct content when the event is processed in a different thread, ensure the event has loaded diagnostic context via LoadDC().
requirements: dest: must be a valid LogString to which text can be appended.
For cross-thread or deferred processing, LoadDC() must have been called on this event to ensure correct NDC content.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEvent::getMDC
functions.signature: bool LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEvent::getMDC(const LogString& key, LogString& dest) const
functions.description: Appends to dest the value associated with the mapped diagnostic context (MDC) key. Returns true if dest was modified. To obtain correct content when the event is processed in a different thread, ensure the event has loaded diagnostic context via LoadDC().
requirements: key: the MDC key to look up; must be a valid LogString.
dest: must be a valid LogString to which the value can be appended.
For cross-thread or deferred processing, LoadDC() must have been called on this event to ensure correct MDC content.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEvent::getMDCKeySet
functions.description: Returns the set of keys present in the mapped diagnostic context (MDC) for this event.
requirements: This method does not modify the object and may be called at any time after construction.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEvent::getMDCCopy
functions.description: Deprecated. Obtains a copy of the current thread's diagnostic context data. Use LoadDC() instead to capture diagnostic context for later or cross-thread processing.
requirements: Availability is conditional: only present when LOG4CXX_ABI_VERSION <= 15.
This method does not modify the object.
Prefer calling LoadDC() instead for correctness in deferred or cross-thread scenarios.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEvent::LoadDC
functions.description: Captures a copy of the current thread's diagnostic context (NDC and MDC) into this event. Required to ensure correct diagnostic context is available when the event is stored for later use or processed on another thread (e.g., asynchronous appenders).
requirements: Call this before queuing, deferring, or handing the event to another thread to preserve diagnostic context.
This method does not modify externally visible fields besides storing context; safe to call immediately after event creation.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEvent::getProperty
functions.signature: bool LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEvent::getProperty(const LogString& key, LogString& dest) const
functions.description: Appends to dest the value associated with the event property named key. Returns true if dest was changed.
requirements: key: the property name to retrieve.
dest: must be a valid LogString to which the property value can be appended.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEvent::getPropertyKeySet
functions.description: Returns the set of property keys present on this event.
requirements: This method does not modify the object and may be called at any time after construction.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEvent::setProperty
functions.signature: void LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEvent::setProperty(const LogString& key, const LogString& value)
functions.description: Associates value with the event property named key, adding or replacing the entry on this event.
requirements: key: property name to set.
value: property value to associate with key.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEvent::renderMessage
functions.description: Uses configured renderers to construct/render the message for this event. Call before getRenderedMessage() if you need renderer-processed output immediately.
requirements: No parameters. May be called after message is set to force rendering.

functions.name: AppenderSkeleton::append
functions.signature: virtual void AppenderSkeleton::append(const spi::LoggingEventPtr& event, helpers::Pool& p) = 0
functions.description: Abstract hook method that concrete Appenders must implement to actually write or transmit a logging event. Typically invoked internally by AppenderSkeleton after filtering/threshold checks (via doAppendImpl). Not intended to be called directly by user code.
requirements: Subclasses must implement this method; AppenderSkeleton itself is abstract.
The provided event must be a valid spi::LoggingEventPtr (non-null is implied by typical usage, but not explicitly stated).
The helpers::Pool reference must be a valid, active memory pool/context for any allocations needed during append (implied by log4cxx patterns).

functions.name: AppenderSkeleton::doAppendImpl
functions.signature: void AppenderSkeleton::doAppendImpl(const spi::LoggingEventPtr& event, helpers::Pool& pool)
functions.description: Performs threshold and filter checks for the given event and, if accepted, delegates to the subclass’s append() implementation to output the event.
requirements: Event is checked against the appender’s threshold; events below threshold are ignored (as per class comments).
Event is passed through the configured filter chain; if any attached filter denies the event, it is not appended; if a filter accepts it, append() is called.
Callers should supply a valid helpers::Pool for any temporary allocations used during logging.

functions.name: AppenderSkeleton::isAccepted
functions.description: Returns whether the given event passes the attached filter chain (i.e., no filter denies the event or at least one accepts it), independent of threshold checks.
requirements: Relies on the currently configured filter chain; if none is present, behavior is determined by implementation but generally implies acceptance.
Event must be a valid spi::LoggingEventPtr.

functions.name: AppenderSkeleton::AppenderSkeleton
functions.description: Default constructor for AppenderSkeleton. Initializes the base appender state (filters, layout, error handler, threshold) according to library defaults.
requirements: No parameters. Usable to create an abstract base for derived appenders.

functions.name: AppenderSkeleton::~AppenderSkeleton
functions.description: Virtual destructor for AppenderSkeleton. Ensures proper cleanup via base class destructors and any overridden logic in derived classes.
requirements: Ensure any resources in derived appenders are released in their destructors or close methods.

functions.name: AppenderSkeleton::finalize
functions.description: Finalizes the appender by calling the derived class’s close method. Intended to ensure cleanup before object destruction or shutdown.
requirements: Should be called when the appender is no longer needed to flush/close resources, as it delegates to the derived close().

functions.name: AppenderSkeleton::activateOptions
functions.description: No-op implementation of OptionHandler::activateOptions. Present to satisfy the interface; does nothing in this base class.
requirements: None; calling this has no effect in AppenderSkeleton.

functions.name: AppenderSkeleton::setOption
functions.signature: void AppenderSkeleton::setOption(const LogString& option, const LogString& value) override
functions.description: Sets a configuration option by name. Supported options include Name and Threshold; other options may be ignored by this base class.
requirements: If option is "Name": value is taken as the appender name (any string).
If option is "Threshold": value should be one of {Trace, Debug, Info, Warn, Error, Fatal, Off, All}.
Defaults: Threshold defaults to All if not set (per documentation table).

functions.name: AppenderSkeleton::addFilter
functions.description: Appends a filter to the end of the filter chain for this appender.
requirements: The newFilter is added at the end of the current chain; behavior if null is not specified.
Filters are evaluated in chain order during event acceptance.

functions.name: AppenderSkeleton::clearFilters
functions.description: Clears the appender’s filter chain, removing all attached filters.
requirements: After calling, there will be no filters attached; event acceptance will not be constrained by filters.

functions.name: AppenderSkeleton::getErrorHandler
functions.description: Returns the currently set ErrorHandler for this appender.
requirements: Returned pointer may be null if no error handler has been set (not explicitly stated; callers should handle that possibility).

functions.name: AppenderSkeleton::getFilter
functions.description: Returns the head filter of the appender’s filter chain.
requirements: If no filters are attached, the returned pointer may be null (implied by related getFirstFilter documentation).

functions.name: AppenderSkeleton::getFirstFilter
functions.description: Returns the first filter in the filter chain, or nullptr if no filter is set.
requirements: Caller should handle a nullptr return when no filter is configured.

functions.name: AppenderSkeleton::getLayout
functions.description: Returns the layout associated with this appender, or nullptr if none. Some appenders may not use a layout.
requirements: Caller should handle a nullptr return if no layout is set or if the appender type does not use a layout.

functions.name: AppenderSkeleton::getName
functions.description: Returns the appender’s name.
requirements: No special requirements.

functions.name: AppenderSkeleton::getThreshold
functions.description: Returns the appender’s threshold level which controls which events are processed.
requirements: Returned pointer may be null if no threshold is set, in which case all levels are considered (implied by isAsSevereAsThreshold docs).

functions.name: AppenderSkeleton::isAsSevereAsThreshold
functions.description: Checks whether the given level meets or exceeds the appender’s threshold. If no threshold is set, always returns true.
requirements: Caller must supply a valid LevelPtr for comparison; if level is null, behavior is unspecified in this header.

functions.name: AppenderSkeleton::doAppend
functions.signature: void AppenderSkeleton::doAppend(const spi::LoggingEventPtr& event, helpers::Pool& pool) override
functions.description: Thread-safe entry point to append an event: acquires a lock to prevent concurrent doAppendImpl execution, then delegates to doAppendImpl for filtering and actual append(). Override in derived classes if a different concurrency control is needed.
requirements: Callers should provide a valid event and pool.
This method may block due to internal locking; avoid deadlocks by not calling it while holding locks that could conflict with appender internals.

functions.name: AppenderSkeleton::setErrorHandler
functions.description: Sets the ErrorHandler to be used by this appender for reporting and handling errors during logging.
requirements: Caller should provide a valid ErrorHandlerPtr; behavior for nullptr is not specified.

functions.name: AppenderSkeleton::setLayout
functions.description: Sets the layout to be used by this appender. Some appenders may ignore the layout or have a fixed layout.
requirements: Caller may pass nullptr to clear the layout (implied by getLayout docs allowing nullptr).
Derived appenders that require a layout should ensure one is set before logging.

functions.name: AppenderSkeleton::setName
functions.description: Sets the appender’s name.
requirements: Name can be any string (per setOption docs for Name).

functions.name: AppenderSkeleton::setThreshold
functions.description: Sets the threshold level; events with lower level than the threshold are ignored by this appender. In configuration, this corresponds to the Threshold option (e.g., "DEBUG", "INFO").
requirements: Caller provides a LevelPtr representing the desired threshold; passing a null pointer removes the threshold so that all events are eligible (inferred from isAsSevereAsThreshold description that no threshold means always true).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Appender::~Appender
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the Appender interface. Ensures proper cleanup via base-class pointers. Implementations may release resources in their own destructors or in close().
requirements: Do not use the object after it has been destroyed.
If called through a base pointer, the destructor must be virtual (it is).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Appender::addFilter
functions.description: Adds a filter to the end of the appender’s filter chain. Filters are evaluated in the order they are added.
requirements: Filters are ordered; this call appends to the end of the list.
Behavior when newFilter is null is not specified in the header (unknown).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Appender::getFilter
functions.description: Returns the head of the filter chain. The full chain can be traversed from this head via the filter’s linkage. Returns null if no filters are present.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Appender::clearFilters
functions.description: Removes all filters from the appender’s filter chain.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Appender::close
functions.description: Releases any resources held by the appender (files, sockets, etc.). After closing, it is a programming error to append to the appender.
requirements: Must not call doAppend() on an appender after it has been closed.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Appender::doAppend
functions.signature: virtual void LOG4CXX_NS::Appender::doAppend(const LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEventPtr& event, LOG4CXX_NS::helpers::Pool& pool) = 0;
functions.description: Performs the appender-specific logging of a single event. Typically invoked by Logger implementations to emit log output.
requirements: Must not be called on a closed appender (per close() contract).
The event parameter should refer to a valid LoggingEventPtr; nullability behavior is not specified (unknown).
The pool reference must refer to a valid, initialized LOG4CXX_NS::helpers::Pool instance (inferred from type; specific initialization requirements are unknown).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Appender::getName
functions.description: Returns the appender’s unique name used to identify it among other components.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Appender::setLayout
functions.description: Sets the Layout used by this appender to format events prior to output.
requirements: Whether a null layout is permitted is not specified (unknown).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Appender::getLayout
functions.description: Returns the Layout currently configured on this appender.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Appender::setName
functions.description: Sets the appender’s name. The name is used by other components to reference this appender.
requirements: Constraints on name content or emptiness are not specified (unknown).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Appender::requiresLayout
functions.description: Indicates whether this appender requires a Layout to function. Configurators use this to decide if they must configure a layout.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Layout::~Layout
functions.description: Virtual destructor for Layout. Ensures proper cleanup through base-class pointers. Typically invoked automatically when a Layout instance (or derived class) is destroyed.
requirements: Object must be a valid instance of LOG4CXX_NS::Layout or a derived class when destruction occurs.
No explicit caller-side requirements beyond normal C++ object lifetime rules.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Layout::format
functions.signature: virtual void LOG4CXX_NS::Layout::format(LogString& output, const spi::LoggingEventPtr& event, LOG4CXX_NS::helpers::Pool& pool) const = 0;
functions.description: Formats a logging event into a textual representation and appends/writes it into output. This is the core method to implement in custom layouts; appenders call it to render events.
requirements: Must be called with a valid, initialized spi::LoggingEventPtr (non-null).
output must reference a valid LogString to receive the formatted text (caller should ensure it is writable; method may append or assign).
pool must reference a valid LOG4CXX_NS::helpers::Pool for any temporary allocations required by the layout.
This method is pure virtual and must be implemented by derived classes before use.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Layout::getContentType
functions.description: Returns the content type (MIME type) produced by this layout. The base implementation returns "text/plain"; derived layouts may override to return another type (e.g., text/html).
requirements: No arguments; may be called at any time on a valid Layout instance.
Callers should not assume a specific value; consult or override as needed.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Layout::appendHeader
functions.description: Appends a header for the layout’s output to the provided buffer. Base implementation does nothing; derived layouts can add prologues (e.g., HTML table headers). Typically called by appenders before rendering log events.
requirements: output must reference a valid LogString buffer to receive the header text.
p must reference a valid LOG4CXX_NS::helpers::Pool for any required allocations.
May be called zero or one times by an appender at the start of a logging session/output stream; exact calling pattern depends on the appender (not enforced by this API).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Layout::appendFooter
functions.description: Appends a footer for the layout’s output to the provided buffer. Base implementation does nothing; derived layouts can add epilogues (e.g., closing HTML tags). Typically called by appenders after rendering log events.
requirements: output must reference a valid LogString buffer to receive the footer text.
p must reference a valid LOG4CXX_NS::helpers::Pool for any required allocations.
May be called at the end of a logging session/output stream; exact calling pattern depends on the appender (not enforced by this API).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::Layout::ignoresThrowable
functions.description: Indicates whether this layout ignores the throwable contained in a LoggingEvent. Return false if the layout itself renders the exception/stack trace; return true if it does not, so the appender can handle it. SimpleLayout, FMTLayout, and PatternLayout typically return true; others may return false.
requirements: No arguments; may be called at any time on a valid Layout instance.
Derived classes must implement this method to accurately reflect whether they render the throwable.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::PatternLayout::PatternLayout
functions.description: Default constructor for PatternLayout. Per comment, it performs no special initialization. Use setOption("ConversionPattern", ...) or setConversionPattern(...) to configure the output pattern before calling format().
requirements: May be constructed without any prior initialization.
If you plan to customize formatting, set a conversion pattern before first use (via setConversionPattern or setOption).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::PatternLayout::PatternLayout
functions.description: Constructs a PatternLayout initialized with the supplied conversion pattern string. The pattern mixes literal text with conversion specifiers that control how a LoggingEvent is formatted.
requirements: pattern can contain literal text and conversion specifiers as supported by the PatternLayout (e.g., %p, %d{...}, %c, %m, %n, %X{key}, %Y/%y, etc.).
Use valid pattern syntax; otherwise behavior is library-defined (details not specified here).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::PatternLayout::~PatternLayout
functions.description: Destructor for PatternLayout. Cleans up internal resources associated with the layout instance.
requirements: Do not use the object after destruction.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::PatternLayout::setConversionPattern
functions.description: Sets the conversion pattern that controls how LoggingEvent instances are formatted. The pattern is a mix of literals and conversion specifiers (e.g., %p, %d{...}, %c, %m, %n, %X{key}, %J, %Y/%y).
requirements: conversionPattern should follow the PatternLayout syntax described in the documentation (conversion characters, optional format modifiers, and recognized options).
If colors are desired via %Y/%y, ensure any color-related options are configured via setOption before formatting.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::PatternLayout::getConversionPattern
functions.description: Returns the current ConversionPattern string used by this PatternLayout.
requirements: Object must be initialized/constructed.
No additional preconditions.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::PatternLayout::activateOptions
functions.description: Applies any pending options and (per comment) calls createPatternParser. Typically invoked after configuration to finalize the layout’s internal state.
requirements: p must reference a valid helpers::Pool that remains valid for the duration of this call.
Call after setting options (e.g., via setOption) if deferred activation is required by the surrounding framework.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::PatternLayout::setOption
functions.signature: void LOG4CXX_NS::PatternLayout::setOption(const LogString& option, const LogString& value);
functions.description: Sets a named configuration option for the PatternLayout. Supported options include the ConversionPattern and per-level color settings used by the %Y/%y specifiers.
requirements: option must be one of: "ConversionPattern", "FatalColor", "ErrorColor", "WarnColor", "InfoColor", "DebugColor", "TraceColor".
For option == "ConversionPattern": value may be any pattern string composed of literals and supported conversion specifiers.

For color options (FatalColor, ErrorColor, WarnColor, InfoColor, DebugColor, TraceColor): value must be one of: the word "None"; a valid ANSI escape sequence (a string starting with \x1b, or a sequence to which ESC and trailing 'm' will be added if it does not start with \x1b); or a composition of named colors/graphics using the documented mini-language (e.g., fg(blue), bg(red), Bold, Dim, Italic, Underline, Blinking, Inverse, Strikethrough) combined with the '|' separator.
Color names can be wrapped with fg(...) for foreground or bg(...) for background; multiple attributes can be combined with '|'.
The special prefix \x1b will be replaced with the ESC character; if a value does not begin with \x1b, ESC and a trailing 'm' will be added automatically.
Option name matching specifics (case sensitivity) are not stated; follow library conventions (unknown in this header).
Call activateOptions if your environment requires explicit activation after setting options.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::PatternLayout::ignoresThrowable

functions.description: Resets the default hierarchy to its default configuration (equivalent to Logger::getDefaultHierarchy()->resetConfiguration()). Use to clear prior configuration and return to defaults.
