functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::DefaultConfigurator::configure
functions.description: Configures the given LoggerRepository from environment settings and configuration files. If setConfigurationFileName() was not called, the configurator uses LOG4CXX_CONFIGURATION or log4j.configuration (with ${varname} expansion using environment variables or spi::Configurator::properties). If no name is provided or found, default candidate files (log4cxx/log4j with .xml/.properties) in the current directory are searched. Uses a custom configurator class if specified by LOG4CXX_CONFIGURATOR_CLASS or log4j.configuratorClass; otherwise, uses PropertyConfigurator unless the file ends with .xml, in which case DOMConfigurator is used. If setConfigurationWatchSeconds() or LOG4CXX_CONFIGURATION_WATCH_SECONDS specifies a positive interval, a background watcher thread is started. Call repository->isConfigured() to determine whether a configuration was applied.
requirements: repository must refer to a valid LoggerRepository object (non-null, initialized).
Callers should inspect repository->isConfigured() after return to determine whether a configuration file was found and applied.
If a custom configurator is desired, set LOG4CXX_CONFIGURATOR_CLASS or log4j.configuratorClass to the fully qualified class name implementing spi::Configurator before calling.
If a specific configuration file should be used, call setConfigurationFileName() before calling configure().
To enable periodic reloads, call setConfigurationWatchSeconds() with a positive value (or set LOG4CXX_CONFIGURATION_WATCH_SECONDS) before calling configure().

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::DefaultConfigurator::tryConfigure
functions.description: Attempts to configure the default LoggerRepository using the same resolution rules as configure(). Returns a status indicating success/failure.
requirements: Caller must check the returned spi::ConfigurationStatus to determine whether configuration succeeded.
Environment variables and prior calls to setConfigurationFileName()/setConfigurationWatchSeconds() influence behavior as described for configure().

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::DefaultConfigurator::setConfigurationFileName
functions.description: Sets the configuration file path used by subsequent configure()/tryConfigure() calls. The path may contain ${varname} placeholders, which are expanded using environment variables if present, otherwise using spi::Configurator::properties.
requirements: Call before configure()/tryConfigure() for the setting to take effect.
path may include ${varname} placeholders that should correspond to either environment variables or keys in spi::Configurator::properties.
If path is invalid or the referenced file is unusable, configuration may fail; callers should verify success via repository->isConfigured() or the return of tryConfigure()/configureFromFile().

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::DefaultConfigurator::setConfigurationWatchSeconds
functions.description: Sets the polling interval for a background thread that watches the configuration file for changes. A positive value starts periodic checks; non-positive values imply no periodic checking.
requirements: Call before configure()/tryConfigure() for the watcher to be started with the given interval.
seconds > 0 enables a background watcher thread; seconds <= 0 results in no periodic watch being started.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::DefaultConfigurator::configureFromFile
functions.signature: static std::tuple<LOG4CXX_NS::spi::ConfigurationStatus, LOG4CXX_NS::LogString> LOG4CXX_NS::DefaultConfigurator::configureFromFile(const std::vector<LOG4CXX_NS::LogString>& directories, const std::vector<LOG4CXX_NS::LogString>& filenames)
functions.description: Builds a combinatorial set of candidate configuration paths from each directory x each filename, expanding ${varname} placeholders, and for the first existing, usable file sets it via setConfigurationFileName() and calls configure() on the default repository. Continues trying remaining candidates if a file exists but cannot be used. Returns the configuration status and the path that was used (if found).
requirements: directories contains directory candidates; filenames contains file-name candidates; both may include ${varname} placeholders for environment variables or spi::Configurator::properties.
Order of search follows the order of elements in directories, then filenames, trying each combination in sequence.
Caller must examine the returned spi::ConfigurationStatus to determine success; the returned LogString path is only meaningful when status indicates success.

requirements: Avoid using the resulting reference if the instance is empty; operations on an empty LoggerPtr may be invalid depending on usage.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::LoggerInstancePtr::get
functions.description: Returns the raw Logger pointer managed by the LoggerPtr. Returns nullptr if the instance is empty.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::LoggerInstancePtr::get

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::NDC::NDC
functions.description: RAII helper that pushes message onto the current thread’s Nested Diagnostic Context (NDC) upon construction and automatically pops it when the object goes out of scope (destructor). Use to bracket a scope so that all log events within include the given context.
requirements: message may be any string; no format is enforced
A per-thread NDC stack is used; effects are confined to the calling thread
Ensure object lifetime matches the intended contextual scope; destruction will pop one level

functions.description: Destructor for the RAII helper; pops one entry from the calling thread’s NDC that was pushed by the constructor. Used to automatically clean up the NDC when leaving scope.

Destruction occurs once; it removes a single matching push

requirements: Affects only the calling thread’s NDC

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::NDC::cloneStack
functions.description: Creates and returns a heap-allocated clone of the calling thread’s NDC stack, typically to pass to another thread for inheritance.
requirements: Return value is never null per docs; treat as non-null
Caller is responsible for deleting the returned Stack unless it is passed to NDC::inherit (which deletes it)
Captures the calling thread’s current NDC state at call time

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::NDC::inherit
functions.description: Replaces the calling thread’s NDC with a clone of the provided parent thread’s NDC. Deletes the provided stack during the call. If stack is NULL, the NDC is not modified.
requirements: stack should be a Stack previously obtained via NDC::cloneStack (or equivalent)
This function deletes stack during the call; the caller must not use or delete it afterward
If stack is NULL, the call is a no-op
Affects only the calling (child) thread’s NDC; the parent’s NDC remains independent after cloning

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::NDC::get
functions.description: Appends the current thread’s full NDC content to dest. Returns true if the NDC is set (non-empty). Intended for layouts to retrieve the composed context string.
requirements: dest is appended to, not cleared; ensure caller handles existing content appropriately
Affects only the calling thread’s NDC state (read-only)

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::NDC::getDepth
functions.description: Returns the current nesting depth (number of entries) of the calling thread’s NDC stack.
requirements: Affects and reflects only the calling thread’s NDC

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::NDC::empty
functions.description: Returns true if the calling thread’s NDC stack is empty.
requirements: Affects and reflects only the calling thread’s NDC

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::NDC::pop
functions.description: Removes and returns the top (most recently pushed) value from the calling thread’s NDC. If the NDC is empty, returns an empty string.
requirements: Affects only the calling thread’s NDC
Caller should handle the empty-string case when no context is available

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::NDC::peek
functions.description: Returns the top value of the calling thread’s NDC without removing it. If empty, returns an empty string.
requirements: Affects only the calling thread’s NDC
Caller should handle the empty-string case when no context is available

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::NDC::push
functions.description: Pushes message onto the calling thread’s NDC stack. The content is user-defined and will appear in layouts that include NDC.
requirements: message may be any string
Affects only the calling thread’s NDC

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::NDC::pushLS
functions.description: Pushes a LogString message onto the calling thread’s NDC. Use when working directly with log4cxx’s LogString type.
requirements: message may be any LogString
Affects only the calling thread’s NDC

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::NDC::remove
functions.description: Removes all diagnostic context data for the calling thread. Threads that push to the NDC should call this before exiting to avoid unbounded memory usage.
requirements: Should be called by threads that have performed unmatched push operations before thread exit
Affects only the calling thread’s NDC

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::NDC::getMessage
functions.signature: static const LogString& LOG4CXX_NS::NDC::getMessage(const LOG4CXX_NS::NDC::DiagnosticContext& ctx)
functions.description: Returns the message component (the pushed value) from a DiagnosticContext pair.
requirements: ctx must be a valid DiagnosticContext obtained from the NDC implementation

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::NDC::getFullMessage
functions.signature: static const LogString& LOG4CXX_NS::NDC::getFullMessage(const LOG4CXX_NS::NDC::DiagnosticContext& ctx)
functions.description: Returns the full message (composed/accumulated message field) from a DiagnosticContext pair.
requirements: ctx must be a valid DiagnosticContext obtained from the NDC implementation

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::MDC::MDC
functions.signature: LOG4CXX_NS::MDC::MDC(const std::string& key, const std::string& value)
functions.description: RAII helper that inserts a key/value into the thread-local Mapped Diagnostic Context (MDC) on construction and removes that key on destruction. Use to scope a context value to a block in the same thread.
requirements: Construction and destruction are expected to occur on the same thread.
Key and value must be valid std::string objects (may be empty).
The MDC is per-thread; effects do not cross threads.
Relies on internal LOG4CXX MDC infrastructure being initialized by the library.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::MDC::~MDC
functions.description: Destructor that removes the key inserted by this MDC instance from the thread-local MDC. Completes RAII lifetime of a scoped MDC entry.
requirements: Must be called on the same thread where the corresponding constructor ran (i.e., object should not outlive its creating thread).
No exceptions are specified; caller should not rely on exceptions from destructor.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::MDC::put
functions.signature: static void LOG4CXX_NS::MDC::put(const std::string& key, const std::string& value)
functions.description: Associates key with value in the current thread's MDC, creating the thread-local map if needed. Subsequent log events in this thread can include this context.
requirements: Callable from any thread; affects only the calling thread's MDC.
Key and value must be valid std::string objects (may be empty).
If a previous value exists for key, it will be overwritten.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::MDC::putLS
functions.signature: static void LOG4CXX_NS::MDC::putLS(const LogString& key, const LogString& value)
functions.description: Sets key/value in the calling thread's MDC using LogString (log4cxx's internal string type), creating the map if needed.
requirements: Affects only the calling thread's MDC.
Key and value must be valid LogString instances (may be empty).
Overwrites any existing value for the key.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::MDC::get
functions.description: Returns the value associated with key in the calling thread's MDC as a std::string. Returns an empty string if not set. No side effects.
requirements: Affects/queries only the calling thread's MDC.
Key must be a valid std::string (may be empty).
Caller should interpret empty return as either unset or explicitly set to empty.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::MDC::remove
functions.description: Removes key from the calling thread's MDC and returns its previous value as std::string. Returns empty if the key was not set.
requirements: Affects only the calling thread's MDC.
Key must be a valid std::string.
Caller should interpret empty return as either unset or previously set to empty.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::MDC::remove
functions.description: Wide-character overload: removes key from the calling thread's MDC and returns its previous value as std::wstring. Returns empty if not set.
requirements: Only available when LOG4CXX_WCHAR_T_API is defined at compile time.
Affects only the calling thread's MDC.
Key must be a valid std::wstring.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::MDC::clear
functions.description: Clears all entries from the calling thread's MDC. Intended to be called before a thread exits to avoid unbounded memory usage.
requirements: Affects only the calling thread's MDC.
Should be called by threads that added entries with put/RAII to avoid memory growth.
Safe to call even if the MDC is empty.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::PropertyConfigurator::PropertyConfigurator
functions.description: Default constructor for PropertyConfigurator. Prepares an instance capable of configuring log4cxx components from properties or a configuration file. Typically followed by calling doConfigure(...). No parameters or side effects are documented.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::PropertyConfigurator::~PropertyConfigurator
functions.description: Virtual destructor for PropertyConfigurator. Cleans up resources held by the configurator instance. No specific usage beyond normal object lifetime management is documented.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::PropertyConfigurator::doConfigure
functions.description: Reads configuration from configFileName and applies it to the specified LoggerRepository. Existing configuration is not cleared or reset; call spi::LoggerRepository::resetConfiguration() first if a reset is desired. This is the ABI <= 15 signature.
requirements: configFileName must refer to a readable configuration file in key=value format as described in PropertyConfigurator_details.
repository must be a valid (non-null) LoggerRepositoryPtr when using this ABI (<= 15).
The existing repository configuration is left intact unless the caller resets it explicitly before calling this function.
Callers should handle the returned spi::ConfigurationStatus to detect success or failure.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::PropertyConfigurator::doConfigure
functions.signature: spi::ConfigurationStatus LOG4CXX_NS::PropertyConfigurator::doConfigure(const File& configFileName, const spi::LoggerRepositoryPtr& repository = spi::LoggerRepositoryPtr())
functions.description: Reads configuration from configFileName and applies it to the provided repository if non-null; otherwise uses the repository held by LogManager. Existing configuration is not cleared or reset; call spi::LoggerRepository::resetConfiguration() first if a reset is desired. This is the ABI > 15 signature.
requirements: configFileName must refer to a readable configuration file in key=value format as described in PropertyConfigurator_details.
If repository is provided, it must point to a valid LoggerRepository instance; if not provided (null), the LogManager-held repository is used.
The existing repository configuration is left intact unless the caller resets it explicitly before calling this function.
Callers should handle the returned spi::ConfigurationStatus to detect success or failure.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::PropertyConfigurator::configure
functions.description: Static helper that reads configuration options from configFilename and applies them to the spi::LoggerRepository held by LogManager. Convenience wrapper around doConfigure using the default repository.
requirements: configFilename must be a readable configuration file in key=value format as described in PropertyConfigurator_details.
The function uses the repository held by LogManager; any existing configuration is not cleared unless the application resets it beforehand.
Callers should handle the returned spi::ConfigurationStatus to detect success or failure.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::PropertyConfigurator::configure
functions.description: Static helper that reads configuration options from a Properties object and applies them to the spi::LoggerRepository held by LogManager. Format is the same as described in PropertyConfigurator_details.
requirements: properties must contain keys and values formatted per PropertyConfigurator_details (e.g., log4j.rootLogger, log4j.appender.*, etc.).
Callers should handle the returned spi::ConfigurationStatus to detect success or failure.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::PropertyConfigurator::configureAndWatch
functions.description: Static helper (available only for LOG4CXX_ABI_VERSION <= 15) that behaves like configureAndWatch(const File&, long) but uses helpers::FileWatchdog::DEFAULT_DELAY for the polling interval. Reads configuration from configFilename and starts a background thread to watch for creation or modification and reconfigure on changes.
requirements: This overload exists only when LOG4CXX_ABI_VERSION <= 15.
configFilename must be a path to a configuration file in key=value format; if the file does not exist initially, it will be read when created.
A background watchdog thread is created and will be stopped by LogManager::shutdown.
Callers should handle the returned spi::ConfigurationStatus to detect success or failure.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::xml::DOMConfigurator::~DOMConfigurator
functions.description: Destructor for DOMConfigurator. Cleans up any resources owned by the configurator instance. No parameters or return value.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::xml::DOMConfigurator::DOMConfigurator
functions.description: Default constructor for DOMConfigurator. Creates an instance capable of configuring Log4cxx from an XML DOM or file.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::xml::DOMConfigurator::DOMConfigurator
functions.description: Constructs a DOMConfigurator associated with the provided memory Pool. Intended for use within Log4cxx internals where APR pools are managed. External behavior beyond construction is not documented in this header.
requirements: Argument p must be a valid LOG4CXX_NS::helpers::Pool reference that remains valid for any operations that depend on it (inferred from usage pattern).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::xml::DOMConfigurator::configure
functions.description: Static convenience overload that interprets filename as an XML file and configures Log4cxx accordingly. This inline overload forwards to the std::string overload.
requirements: filename must point to a null-terminated path to an XML configuration file.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::xml::DOMConfigurator::configure
functions.description: Static method that interprets filename as an XML file and configures Log4cxx accordingly. Existing configuration is not cleared/reset by this call.
requirements: filename must refer to a configuration file in XML format.
If a reset of existing configuration is required, caller must invoke spi::LoggerRepository::resetConfiguration before calling this (see doConfigure notes).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::xml::DOMConfigurator::configure
functions.description: Static method (available when LOG4CXX_WCHAR_T_API is enabled) that interprets a wide-character filename as an XML file and configures Log4cxx.
requirements: Requires LOG4CXX_WCHAR_T_API to be enabled at build time.
filename must point to a null-terminated wide-character path to an XML configuration file.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::xml::DOMConfigurator::configure
functions.description: Static method (available when LOG4CXX_WCHAR_T_API is enabled) that interprets a wide-string filename as an XML file and configures Log4cxx.
requirements: Requires LOG4CXX_WCHAR_T_API to be enabled at build time.
filename must refer to a configuration file in XML format.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::xml::DOMConfigurator::configure
functions.description: Static method (available when LOG4CXX_UNICHAR_API or LOG4CXX_LOGCHAR_IS_UNICHAR is enabled) that interprets a UniChar string filename as an XML file and configures Log4cxx.
requirements: Requires LOG4CXX_UNICHAR_API or LOG4CXX_LOGCHAR_IS_UNICHAR to be enabled at build time.
filename must refer to a configuration file in XML format.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::xml::DOMConfigurator::configureAndWatch
functions.description: Reads the XML configuration file if it exists and starts a background thread that periodically checks the file for creation or modification using a default delay (helpers::FileWatchdog::DEFAULT_DELAY). On change, the file is re-read to reconfigure Log4cxx. The thread stops on LogManager::shutdown.
requirements: configFilename must refer to a configuration file in XML format.
A background thread is created; the application must tolerate asynchronous reconfiguration.
The monitoring thread is terminated by LogManager::shutdown.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::xml::DOMConfigurator::configureAndWatch
functions.description: Wide-string variant (available when LOG4CXX_WCHAR_T_API is enabled). Reads the configuration and starts a background watcher using the default delay.
requirements: Requires LOG4CXX_WCHAR_T_API to be enabled at build time.
configFilename must refer to a configuration file in XML format.
The monitoring thread is terminated by LogManager::shutdown.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::xml::DOMConfigurator::configureAndWatch
functions.description: UniChar-string variant (available when LOG4CXX_UNICHAR_API or LOG4CXX_LOGCHAR_IS_UNICHAR is enabled). Reads the configuration and starts a background watcher using the default delay.
requirements: Requires LOG4CXX_UNICHAR_API or LOG4CXX_LOGCHAR_IS_UNICHAR to be enabled at build time.
configFilename must refer to a configuration file in XML format.
The monitoring thread is terminated by LogManager::shutdown.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::xml::DOMConfigurator::configureAndWatch
functions.description: CFStringRef variant (available when LOG4CXX_CFSTRING_API is enabled). Reads the configuration and starts a background watcher using the default delay.
requirements: Requires LOG4CXX_CFSTRING_API to be enabled at build time.
configFilename must refer to a configuration file in XML format.
The monitoring thread is terminated by LogManager::shutdown.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::xml::DOMConfigurator::configureAndWatch
functions.signature: static LOG4CXX_NS::spi::ConfigurationStatus LOG4CXX_NS::xml::DOMConfigurator::configureAndWatch(const std::string& configFilename, long delay)
functions.description: Reads the XML configuration file if it exists and starts a background thread that checks the file for creation/modification every delay milliseconds. On change, the file is re-read to reconfigure Log4cxx. The thread stops on LogManager::shutdown.
requirements: configFilename must refer to a configuration file in XML format.
delay is the period in milliseconds between checks; it must be a non-negative integer (negative values are not documented as valid).
A background thread is created; the application must tolerate asynchronous reconfiguration.
The monitoring thread is terminated by LogManager::shutdown.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::xml::DOMConfigurator::configureAndWatch
functions.signature: static LOG4CXX_NS::spi::ConfigurationStatus LOG4CXX_NS::xml::DOMConfigurator::configureAndWatch(const std::wstring& configFilename, long delay)
functions.description: Wide-string variant (available when LOG4CXX_WCHAR_T_API is enabled) that starts a background watcher with the specified delay in milliseconds.
requirements: Requires LOG4CXX_WCHAR_T_API to be enabled at build time.
configFilename must refer to a configuration file in XML format.
delay is the period in milliseconds between checks; it must be a non-negative integer.
The monitoring thread is terminated by LogManager::shutdown.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::xml::DOMConfigurator::configureAndWatch
functions.signature: static LOG4CXX_NS::spi::ConfigurationStatus LOG4CXX_NS::xml::DOMConfigurator::configureAndWatch(const std::basic_string<UniChar>& configFilename, long delay)
functions.description: UniChar-string variant (available when LOG4CXX_UNICHAR_API or LOG4CXX_LOGCHAR_IS_UNICHAR is enabled) that starts a background watcher with the specified delay in milliseconds.
requirements: Requires LOG4CXX_UNICHAR_API or LOG4CXX_LOGCHAR_IS_UNICHAR to be enabled at build time.
configFilename must refer to a configuration file in XML format.
delay is the period in milliseconds between checks; it must be a non-negative integer.
The monitoring thread is terminated by LogManager::shutdown.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::xml::DOMConfigurator::configureAndWatch
functions.signature: static LOG4CXX_NS::spi::ConfigurationStatus LOG4CXX_NS::xml::DOMConfigurator::configureAndWatch(const CFStringRef& configFilename, long delay)
functions.description: CFStringRef variant (available when LOG4CXX_CFSTRING_API is enabled) that starts a background watcher with the specified delay in milliseconds.
requirements: Requires LOG4CXX_CFSTRING_API to be enabled at build time.
configFilename must refer to a configuration file in XML format.
delay is the period in milliseconds between checks; it must be a non-negative integer.
The monitoring thread is terminated by LogManager::shutdown.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::xml::DOMConfigurator::doConfigure
functions.description: Interprets filename as an XML file and configures Log4cxx accordingly, storing Logger instances in the provided repository. The existing configuration is not cleared nor reset by this call. If a different behavior is required, call spi::LoggerRepository::resetConfiguration before calling doConfigure.
requirements: filename must refer to the XML file to parse.
repository must be a valid LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggerRepositoryPtr instance.
This overload is available when LOG4CXX_ABI_VERSION <= 15 (per header conditions).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::xml::XMLLayout::XMLLayout
functions.description: Constructs an XMLLayout that formats logging events as log4j:event XML fragments. By default, location info and MDC properties are disabled.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::xml::XMLLayout::~XMLLayout
functions.description: Destructor for XMLLayout. Cleans up any internal resources. Typical usage is automatic via RAII when the layout goes out of scope or is released by an appender.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::xml::XMLLayout::setLocationInfo
functions.description: Enables or disables inclusion of file name and line number (location info) in the XML output for each event.
requirements: > locationInfo1: boolean flag indicating whether to include location info (true to include, false to omit).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::xml::XMLLayout::getLocationInfo
functions.description: Returns whether location info (file and line number) is currently included in the XML output.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::xml::XMLLayout::setProperties
functions.description: Enables or disables output of MDC (mapped diagnostic context) key-value pairs in the XML output. Default is disabled.
requirements: > flag: boolean flag indicating whether to include MDC properties (true to include, false to omit).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::xml::XMLLayout::getProperties
functions.description: Returns whether MDC key-value pairs are currently included in the XML output.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::xml::XMLLayout::activateOptions
functions.description: No-op for XMLLayout. Present to satisfy OptionHandler; calling it performs no action.
requirements: > p: must be a valid helpers::Pool reference if provided; it is unused.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::xml::XMLLayout::setOption
functions.signature: void LOG4CXX_NS::xml::XMLLayout::setOption(const LOG4CXX_NS::LogString& option, const LOG4CXX_NS::LogString& value);
functions.description: Sets a configuration option by name. Supported options are "Properties" (include MDC key-value pairs) and "LocationInfo" (include file and line number). Values are boolean-like strings per documentation.
requirements: > option: must be one of "Properties" or "LocationInfo" to have effect.
value: must be "True" or "False" (per documented supported values).
Unsupported option names may be ignored without effect.
Default for both options is False if not set.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::xml::XMLLayout::format
functions.signature: void LOG4CXX_NS::xml::XMLLayout::format(LOG4CXX_NS::LogString& output, const LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEventPtr& event, LOG4CXX_NS::helpers::Pool& p) const;
functions.description: Formats a LoggingEvent into a log4j:event XML fragment conforming to log4cxx.dtd, appending it to output. Respects the LocationInfo and Properties settings and includes throwable information (exceptions) in the output.
requirements: > output: must be a valid LogString reference that can be appended to.
event: should reference a valid (non-null) spi::LoggingEventPtr containing the event to format.
p: must be a valid helpers::Pool reference for any internal allocations required during formatting.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::xml::XMLLayout::ignoresThrowable
functions.description: Indicates whether the layout ignores throwable information. Always returns false, meaning exceptions are included in the formatted output.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SMTPAppender::SMTPAppender
functions.description: Default constructor. Creates an SMTPAppender configured with a default spi::TriggeringEventEvaluator that triggers on events at level ERROR or higher. Use setters or setOption/activateOptions to complete configuration before logging.
requirements: After configuring properties, callers should invoke activateOptions(helpers::Pool&) before the appender is used to log events.
A Layout must be set before activation; otherwise activateOptions will fail.
A TriggeringEventEvaluator must be present (the default is provided by this constructor).
Required SMTP fields (smtpHost, from, and at least one of to/cc/bcc) must be provided before activation.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SMTPAppender::SMTPAppender
functions.description: Constructs an SMTPAppender using the provided memory Pool. Uses the default TriggeringEventEvaluator (triggers on ERROR or higher). Configuration must still be completed (e.g., SMTP host, recipients) and activated before use.
requirements: The provided LOG4CXX_NS::helpers::Pool& p must be valid and remain alive for the duration of construction.
After configuring properties, callers should invoke activateOptions(helpers::Pool&) before the appender is used to log events.
A Layout must be set before activation; otherwise activateOptions will fail.
Required SMTP fields (smtpHost, from, and at least one of to/cc/bcc) must be provided before activation.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SMTPAppender::SMTPAppender
functions.description: Constructs an SMTPAppender using the provided TriggeringEventEvaluator instance to decide when to send an email. Configuration (SMTP fields, layout, etc.) must be completed and activated before use.
requirements: The evaluator pointer should refer to a valid instance implementing spi::TriggeringEventEvaluator.
After configuring properties, callers should invoke activateOptions(helpers::Pool&) before the appender is used to log events.
A Layout must be set before activation; otherwise activateOptions will fail.
Required SMTP fields (smtpHost, from, and at least one of to/cc/bcc) must be provided before activation.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SMTPAppender::~SMTPAppender
functions.description: Destructor for SMTPAppender. Releases resources associated with the appender.
requirements: The appender should be closed() before destruction if the lifecycle requires flushing or resource release; otherwise unknown (not explicitly documented).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SMTPAppender::setOption
functions.signature: void LOG4CXX_NS::net::SMTPAppender::setOption(const LogString& option, const LogString& value)
functions.description: Sets a configuration option by name. Supported keys include smtpHost, smtpPort, smtpUserName, smtpPassword, from, to, cc, bcc, subject, buffersize, evaluatorClass. Values are parsed and stored; activation is deferred to activateOptions.
requirements: Option names must match supported keys; unsupported options will be ignored or handled by base class (per AppenderSkeleton::setOption).
Fields from, to, cc, bcc must contain only ASCII characters; non-ASCII will prevent activation.
buffersize should be an integer; the default is 512 if unspecified.
smtpPort should be an integer; the default is 25 if unspecified.
An evaluatorClass must refer to a registered class deriving from spi::TriggeringEventEvaluator if provided.
Changes take effect after calling activateOptions(helpers::Pool&).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SMTPAppender::activateOptions
functions.description: Validates and applies the current configuration. Will log an error and not activate if required fields are missing, layout is absent, evaluator is missing, or non-ASCII characters are present where not permitted.
requirements: A valid LOG4CXX_NS::helpers::Pool& p must be provided.
A Layout must be set prior to activation.
A TriggeringEventEvaluator must be set (or present by default).
Required fields must be provided: smtpHost, from, and at least one of to, cc, or bcc.
Fields from, to, cc, and bcc must contain only ASCII characters.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SMTPAppender::append
functions.description: Appends a logging event: stores it in the cyclic buffer and, if the configured TriggeringEventEvaluator signals a trigger, sends an email with the buffered events.
requirements: activateOptions must have succeeded prior to calling append; otherwise sending will not occur and errors may be logged.
event must be a valid LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEventPtr.
A valid LOG4CXX_NS::helpers::Pool& p must be supplied.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SMTPAppender::close
functions.description: Closes the appender, releasing resources. After close, no further events should be appended.
requirements: Should be safe to call multiple times; specific behavior not documented.
Do not call append() after close().

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SMTPAppender::getTo
functions.description: Returns the current value of the To option (comma-separated list of recipient email addresses).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SMTPAppender::getCc
functions.description: Returns the current value of the Cc option (comma-separated list of CC recipient email addresses).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SMTPAppender::getBcc
functions.description: Returns the current value of the Bcc option (comma-separated list of BCC recipient email addresses).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SMTPAppender::requiresLayout
functions.description: Indicates that this appender requires a Layout.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SMTPAppender::sendBuffer
functions.description: Sends the current contents of the cyclic buffer as an email message using the configured SMTP settings.

Non-ASCII characters are not permitted in from/to/cc/bcc.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SMTPAppender::getEvaluatorClass
functions.description: Returns the configured evaluator class name (EvaluatorClass option), if any.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SMTPAppender::getFrom
functions.description: Returns the From email address.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SMTPAppender::getSubject
functions.description: Returns the email Subject text.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SMTPAppender::setFrom
functions.description: Sets the From email address for outgoing messages.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SMTPAppender::setSubject
functions.description: Sets the Subject line for outgoing messages.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SMTPAppender::setBufferSize
functions.description: Sets the maximum number of logging events to retain in the cyclic buffer. Oldest events are discarded when the limit is reached. Default is 512.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SMTPAppender::setSMTPHost

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SMTPAppender::getSMTPHost
functions.description: Returns the configured SMTP server host name or IP address.

functions.description: Sets the SMTP server TCP port. Default is 25 if not set via options.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SMTPAppender::getSMTPPort
functions.description: Returns the configured SMTP server TCP port.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SMTPAppender::setTo
functions.description: Sets the To recipients as a comma-separated list of email addresses.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SMTPAppender::setCc
functions.description: Sets the Cc recipients as a comma-separated list of email addresses.
requirements: Only ASCII characters are permitted in this field.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SMTPAppender::setBcc
functions.description: Sets the Bcc recipients as a comma-separated list of email addresses.
requirements: Only ASCII characters are permitted in this field.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SMTPAppender::setSMTPUsername
functions.description: Sets the SMTP server user name for authentication, if required by the server.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SMTPAppender::getSMTPUsername
functions.description: Returns the configured SMTP user name.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SMTPAppender::setSMTPPassword
functions.description: Sets the SMTP server password for authentication, if required by the server.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SMTPAppender::getSMTPPassword
functions.description: Returns the configured SMTP password.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SMTPAppender::getBufferSize
functions.description: Returns the current cyclic buffer size (maximum number of retained events).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SMTPAppender::getEvaluator
functions.description: Returns the currently configured TriggeringEventEvaluator.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SMTPAppender::setEvaluator
functions.description: Sets the TriggeringEventEvaluator used to decide when to send emails.
requirements: trigger must reference a valid object implementing spi::TriggeringEventEvaluator.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SyslogAppender::SyslogAppender

A layout must be set on the appender before calling (requiresLayout() returns true).
Syslog host must be configured via setSyslogHost(); if not set, the appender will fail.
MaxMessageLength controls splitting; default is 1024 unless changed via setMaxMessageLength().
Pool p must be a valid helpers::Pool instance for any internal allocations.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SyslogAppender::activateOptions

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SyslogAppender::getSyslogHost

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SyslogAppender::setFacility
functions.description: Sets the syslog facility using a textual name.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::SyslogAppender::getMaxMessageLength

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::TelnetAppender::TelnetAppender
functions.description: Constructs a TelnetAppender that can accept TCP clients and stream log events to them. Configure options (port, hostname, encoding, max connections, reuse-address) via setters or setOption(), then call activateOptions() to start listening.
requirements: Must be configured (via setPort, setHostname, setEncoding, setMaxConnections, setReuseAddress, or setOption) before activateOptions() for settings to take effect.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::TelnetAppender::~TelnetAppender
functions.description: Destructor. Shuts down internal resources associated with the TelnetAppender (e.g., listener socket and client connections). Typically invoked through close() or when the object goes out of scope.
requirements: Do not use the appender after destruction.
If managed polymorphically through base-class pointers, ensure close() is called before destruction if required by the surrounding system.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::TelnetAppender::requiresLayout
functions.description: Indicates whether this appender requires a layout. For TelnetAppender, if no layout is provided, only the raw log message is sent to connected clients.
requirements: None; callable at any time to query behavior.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::TelnetAppender::getEncoding
functions.description: Returns the current character encoding used to transmit log messages to clients.
requirements: None; safe to call to inspect current configuration.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::TelnetAppender::setEncoding
functions.description: Sets the character encoding used to send log data to clients. Supported encodings include UTF-8 (default), UTF-16 variants, US-ASCII and ISO-8859-1, among others listed in the header comments.

Call before activateOptions() to ensure it applies when the listener starts.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::TelnetAppender::activateOptions
functions.description: Initializes and starts the appender: creates the listening socket and begins accepting client connections according to the configured options.
requirements: Should be called after all desired options (port, hostname, encoding, max connections, reuse address) are set.
The provided Pool reference p must be valid for the duration of the call.
Only call once per appender initialization cycle; call close() before re-activating if reconfiguration is needed.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::TelnetAppender::setOption
functions.signature: void LOG4CXX_NS::net::TelnetAppender::setOption(const LOG4CXX_NS::LogString& option, const LOG4CXX_NS::LogString& value)
functions.description: Sets a configuration option by name. Supported options include Port, Hostname, MaxConnections, Encoding, and ReuseAddress as described in the header comments. Values are parsed and applied to the appender’s configuration.
requirements: option must be one of: "Port", "Hostname", "MaxConnections", "Encoding", "ReuseAddress" (matching the documented options).

value must be a valid representation for the chosen option: integer for Port/MaxConnections, hostname or numeric address for Hostname, one of the supported encodings for Encoding, and True/False for ReuseAddress.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::TelnetAppender::getPort
functions.description: Returns the TCP port number the appender is configured to listen on.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::TelnetAppender::setPort
functions.description: Sets the TCP port number on which the appender will accept incoming client connections.

Call before activateOptions() to apply the port setting.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::TelnetAppender::getHostname
functions.description: Returns the hostname/interface on which the appender accepts connections. If unset, the appender listens on all interfaces.
requirements: None.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::TelnetAppender::setHostname
functions.description: Sets the hostname or numeric address on which the appender will bind and accept connections. By default, it accepts connections on any network interface.
requirements: newValue must be a valid local hostname or numeric address (inferred from documentation).
Call before activateOptions() to apply the binding address.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::TelnetAppender::getMaxConnections
functions.description: Returns the configured maximum number of concurrent client connections allowed.
requirements: None.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::TelnetAppender::setMaxConnections
functions.description: Sets the maximum number of concurrent client connections allowed.

Call before activateOptions() for the limit to take effect.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::TelnetAppender::setReuseAddress
functions.description: Enables or disables SO_REUSEADDR on the listening socket. When true, clients can reconnect quickly after the process restarts (e.g., while the socket is in TIME_WAIT).
requirements: Call before activateOptions() so the socket is created with the desired reuse setting.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::net::TelnetAppender::close
functions.description: Shuts down the appender, closing the listening socket and disconnecting clients. After close(), the appender should not be used until reconfigured and re-activated.
requirements: Safe to call when the appender is active; subsequent logging to this appender will be ignored or buffered according to the framework’s behavior.

functions.name: XMLSocketAppender::XMLSocketAppender
functions.description: Default constructor. Creates an XMLSocketAppender instance that can later be configured (e.g., with a remote host/port) and attached to loggers to send LoggingEvent data, typically over TCP. No connection is established by this constructor alone.
requirements: No explicit runtime requirements documented for construction.
The class is non-copyable (copy constructor/operator are private), so do not attempt to copy instances.
Further configuration (e.g., remote host/port or layout) is likely required before use, per class documentation.

functions.name: XMLSocketAppender::XMLSocketAppender
functions.description: Constructor that connects to a remote server at the given network address and TCP port. Intended to start (or prepare) a TCP connection for transmitting LoggingEvent data to a remote log server, usually formatted by the configured layout (e.g., XML/JSON).
requirements: address must reference a valid LOG4CXX_NS::helpers::InetAddress object (non-null).
port is a TCP port number; it should be within the valid range 0..65535 and non-negative (inferred from typical TCP usage).
A reachable server at the specified address:port is required for successful logging; if down, events may be dropped until reconnection (per documentation).
Caller should consider explicitly closing the appender (close()) before shutdown to avoid loss of buffered data.

functions.name: XMLSocketAppender::XMLSocketAppender
functions.description: Constructor that connects to a remote server at the given host name (or IP string) and TCP port. Used to transmit LoggingEvent data over TCP to a remote log server, usually formatted by the configured layout.
requirements: host should be a valid, resolvable host name or IP string; empty strings are invalid (inferred).
port is a TCP port number; it should be within the valid range 0..65535 and non-negative (inferred from typical TCP usage).
Name resolution must succeed for host to connect; if the server is down, events may be dropped until reconnection (per documentation).
Caller should explicitly close the appender (close()) before shutdown to avoid loss of buffered data.

functions.name: XMLSocketAppender::~XMLSocketAppender
functions.description: Destructor. Cleans up the XMLSocketAppender. Per the class documentation, if a background connector thread exists (when the server is down), the appender may not be destroyed until it’s explicitly closed. To avoid loss of untransmitted data and ensure termination of background threads, close the appender before application shutdown.
requirements: Call close() on the appender before application exit to avoid potential data loss and ensure background connector thread termination (per documentation).
Do not rely on implicit destruction while a connector thread is active; explicitly close to guarantee destruction.
The class is non-copyable; ensure you are destroying the original instance, not a copy.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::db::DBAppender::DBAppender

requirements: Must be configured via setOption (or XML configuration) before activateOptions/use.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::db::DBAppender::setOption
functions.signature: void LOG4CXX_NS::db::DBAppender::setOption(const LOG4CXX_NS::LogString& option, const LOG4CXX_NS::LogString& value)
functions.description: Sets a configuration option for the DBAppender. Supported options include DriverName, DriverParams, DatabaseName, SQL, and ColumnMapping. Intended to be called during configuration (e.g., from XML) prior to activation.

Must be called before activateOptions for settings to take effect.
value format/semantics are database/driver specific for DriverParams.

functions.description: Activates the configured options and initializes database-related resources using the provided APR memory Pool. Call after all setOption calls and before logging begins.

p must be a valid LOG4CXX_NS::helpers::Pool reference that remains valid for the duration of the activation call.
Should be called before append is ever invoked.

event should be a valid (non-null) LoggingEventPtr.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::db::DBAppender::close
functions.description: Closes the appender, releasing resources and flushing any buffered events to the database as appropriate. After close, the appender should not be used for further logging.

Call close during shutdown to ensure buffered events are flushed.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::db::DBAppender::requiresLayout

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::db::DBAppender::getSql

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RollingFileAppender::RollingFileAppender
functions.description: Constructor that accepts a private implementation object. Functionally equivalent regarding subsequent configuration and use of the appender.
requirements: priv must point to a valid RollingFileAppender::RollingFileAppenderPriv instance (ownership is transferred).
After constructing, set a RollingPolicy and a TriggeringPolicy (or a RollingPolicy that also implements TriggeringPolicy) for the appender to be useful.
Call activateOptions(...) after configuration to apply options and initialize resources before use.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RollingFileAppender::getMaxBackupIndex
functions.description: Returns the MaxBackupIndex setting, i.e., how many backup files are kept before the oldest is erased. A value of 0 means no backups and truncation on rollover.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RollingFileAppender::getMaximumFileSize
functions.description: Returns the maximum active log file size in bytes before rollover is triggered by size (if a size-based policy is used).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RollingFileAppender::setMaxBackupIndex
functions.description: Sets the maximum number of backup files to keep. If set to zero, no backups are kept and the active log file is truncated on rollover.
requirements: maxBackupIndex must be a non-negative integer.
A value of 0 disables backups and causes truncation on rollover.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RollingFileAppender::setMaxFileSize
functions.description: Sets the maximum active log file size using a human-readable string. Supports numeric values with KB, MB, or GB suffixes. The value is interpreted as bytes if no suffix is provided.
requirements: value must represent a long integer in the range 0 to 2^63, optionally suffixed with KB, MB, or GB (e.g., "10KB" = 10240).
Malformed size strings result in unspecified behavior according to this header (exact error handling unknown).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RollingFileAppender::setMaximumFileSize
functions.description: Sets the maximum active log file size in bytes.
requirements: value must be a non-negative size in bytes.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RollingFileAppender::setDatePattern
functions.description: Sets the date pattern used to determine the rollover schedule. Accepts patterns compatible with java.text.SimpleDateFormat and the special values ABSOLUTE, DATE, or ISO8601.
requirements: pattern must be a SimpleDateFormat-compatible pattern or one of: ABSOLUTE, DATE, ISO8601.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RollingFileAppender::makeFileNamePattern
functions.description: Builds and returns a filename pattern string from the provided date pattern. Typically used to generate FileNamePattern for time-based policies. Detailed formatting is not documented here.
requirements: datePattern should be a SimpleDateFormat-compatible pattern or a supported alias (ABSOLUTE, DATE, ISO8601), consistent with setDatePattern().

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RollingFileAppender::setOption
functions.signature: void LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RollingFileAppender::setOption(const LogString& option, const LogString& value) override
functions.description: Sets a named configuration option on the appender. Supported options include FileDatePattern, MaxBackupIndex, and MaxFileSize. Values follow the documented formats. Intended to be called during configuration prior to activateOptions().
requirements: option must be one of the supported names: FileDatePattern, MaxBackupIndex, MaxFileSize (per this header).
For FileDatePattern, value must be a SimpleDateFormat-compatible pattern or ABSOLUTE, DATE, ISO8601.
For MaxBackupIndex, value should be an integer (documentation table shows supported values 1–12; other uses unspecified here).
For MaxFileSize, value must be an integer 0–2^63 with optional KB, MB, GB suffixes.
Call activateOptions(...) after setting options to apply them.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RollingFileAppender::activateOptions
functions.description: Applies the configured options and prepares the appender for use. Mirrors FileAppender::activateOptions behavior within the rolling context.
requirements: pool must be a valid LOG4CXX_NS::helpers::Pool instance.
Call after all setOption(...) and policy setters, before the appender is used for logging.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RollingFileAppender::rollover
functions.description: Performs a log file rollover according to the configured policies. If MaxBackupIndex > 0, renames File.N to File.N+1, renames current File to File.1, and starts a new File. If MaxBackupIndex == 0, truncates the current file with no backups.
requirements: p must be a valid LOG4CXX_NS::helpers::Pool instance.
Behavior depends on MaxBackupIndex: 0 (truncate, no backups) or positive (rename chain as documented).
Should be invoked when the triggering policy indicates rollover (exact invocation timing is policy-dependent).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RollingFileAppender::getRollingPolicy
functions.description: Returns the RollingPolicy in use, which defines how log files are rolled (naming, retention, compression, etc.).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RollingFileAppender::getTriggeringPolicy
functions.description: Returns the TriggeringPolicy in use, which determines when to trigger a rollover (e.g., size-based or time-based).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RollingFileAppender::setRollingPolicy
functions.description: Sets the RollingPolicy used to roll log files. If the provided policy also implements TriggeringPolicy, it will be used for triggering as well.
requirements: policy should be set before logging begins; for the appender to be useful, a RollingPolicy and a TriggeringPolicy must be configured (or a single policy implementing both).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RollingFileAppender::setTriggeringPolicy
functions.description: Sets the TriggeringPolicy that determines when to trigger rollover events.
requirements: policy should be set before logging begins; ensure either both policies are set or the RollingPolicy also implements TriggeringPolicy.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RollingFileAppender::close
functions.description: Closes the appender and waits for any asynchronous file compression actions to complete.
requirements: Do not attempt to log through this appender after close() has been called.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RollingFileAppender::getFileLength
functions.description: Returns the current byte length of the active log file (tracked/estimated by the appender).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RollingFileAppender::incrementFileLength
functions.description: Increments the internally tracked byte length of the active log file by the specified number of bytes.
requirements: increment must represent the number of additional bytes written; it must be non-negative (type is size_t).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::MultiprocessRollingFileAppender::MultiprocessRollingFileAppender
functions.description: Default constructor for a multiprocess-safe rolling file appender. Creates an instance that coordinates file rollovers across multiple processes. Typical usage: construct, set properties (file name, pattern, policies), then call activateOptions() before logging begins.
requirements: Must be followed by a call to activateOptions(helpers::Pool&) to finalize configuration before the appender is used for logging.
For this class (per header note), the Append option should not be set to false; rolling is only relevant when appending.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::MultiprocessRollingFileAppender::activateOptions
functions.description: Finalize and activate the appender’s configuration (copy of FileAppender::activateOptions behavior), preparing it for use. In this multiprocess variant, activation includes any setup needed to coordinate with other processes before logging or rolling can occur.
requirements: pool must be a valid LOG4CXX_NS::helpers::Pool reference that remains usable for the duration of the activation call.
Call only after setting desired configuration properties (e.g., file name, encoding, policies).
Should be called before any logging occurs with this appender.
For this appender, do not configure Append=false (per class note).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::MultiprocessRollingFileAppender::rollover
functions.description: Perform the usual rolling file behavior for the active log file. If MaxBackupIndex > 0, existing files File.1..File.MaxBackupIndex-1 are renamed to File.2..File.MaxBackupIndex, the current File is renamed to File.1 and closed, and a new File is created for subsequent log output. If MaxBackupIndex == 0, the current File is truncated and no backups are kept. Returns true on successful rollover (and, in the multiprocess context, when this process performed the rollover). Intended to be invoked when the configured triggering policy indicates a roll is needed.
requirements: p must be a valid LOG4CXX_NS::helpers::Pool reference for use during the rollover operation.
Behavior depends on the configured MaxBackupIndex: positive values enable backup rotation; zero truncates without backups (no other values are documented).
The appender should be configured and activated (activateOptions) before calling rollover.
For correct semantics in multiprocess scenarios, use this class with appending enabled (Append must not be false, per class note).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RollingPolicy::~RollingPolicy
functions.description: Virtual destructor for RollingPolicy. Enables safe deletion through base-class pointers for implementations of rolling policies used by rolling file appenders. Typically invoked when the policy is no longer needed.
requirements: Object must be a valid RollingPolicy instance or derived implementation when destroyed.
Do not use the object after destruction (standard C++ object lifetime requirement).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RollingPolicy::initialize
functions.signature: virtual LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RolloverDescriptionPtr initialize(const LOG4CXX_NS::LogString& currentActiveFile, const bool append, LOG4CXX_NS::helpers::Pool& pool) = 0;
functions.description: Initializes the rolling policy and returns any initial rollover actions required by a RollingFileAppender before logging begins. If no initialization is needed, it returns null. May throw SecurityException if access to log files is denied.
requirements: currentActiveFile must be the current value of RollingFileAppender::getFile().
append must be the current value of RollingFileAppender::getAppend().
pool must be a valid memory pool usable for allocations during this call and must remain valid for the duration of the call.
Caller must handle a null return indicating no initialization is needed.
Caller must be prepared to handle a SecurityException if access to log files is denied.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RollingPolicy::rollover
functions.signature: virtual LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RolloverDescriptionPtr rollover(const LOG4CXX_NS::LogString& currentActiveFile, const bool append, LOG4CXX_NS::helpers::Pool& pool) = 0;
functions.description: Prepares for a log file rollover. Called prior to closing the active log file; performs any necessary preliminary actions and returns a description of actions to perform after closing the current file. If no rollover is needed at this time, it returns null. May throw SecurityException if access to log files is denied.
requirements: currentActiveFile must be the file name for the current active log file.
append must be the current value of the parent FileAppender::getAppend().
pool must be a valid memory pool usable for allocations during this call and must remain valid for the duration of the call.
Caller must handle a null return indicating that no rollover should occur at this time.
This method should be called prior to closing the active log file as part of the rollover sequence.
Caller must be prepared to handle a SecurityException if access to log files is denied.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RollingPolicyBase::RollingPolicyBase
functions.description: Default constructor for the abstract rolling policy base class. Initializes common state used by rolling policies. The class is abstract (getFormatSpecifiers is pure virtual) and is intended to be constructed only via derived classes.
requirements: Class is abstract; do not instantiate directly—derive and implement getFormatSpecifiers().

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RollingPolicyBase::~RollingPolicyBase
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the rolling policy base class, enabling safe destruction via base-class pointers in polymorphic use.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RollingPolicyBase::activateOptions
functions.description: Activates the configured options for the rolling policy. Logs a warning if no FileNamePattern has been set. Typically called after options are configured and before the policy is used.

Parameter p must be a valid memory pool reference.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RollingPolicyBase::getFormatSpecifiers
functions.description: Pure-virtual function returning a map of supported pattern format specifiers (e.g., for date or index formatting) for the concrete rolling policy. Used to interpret the FileNamePattern.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RollingPolicyBase::setOption
functions.signature: void LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RollingPolicyBase::setOption(const LOG4CXX_NS::LogString& option, const LOG4CXX_NS::LogString& value)
functions.description: Sets a named configuration option for the rolling policy. Supported options include FileNamePattern and CreateIntermediateDirectories. Values must adhere to the documented constraints; unrecognized options are not described here.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RollingPolicyBase::setFileNamePattern
functions.description: Sets the file name pattern used by the rolling policy to name rolled files. The pattern can include conversion specifiers supported by the concrete policy (e.g., date or index specifiers).
requirements: fnp should contain only legal file name characters plus conversion specifiers supported by the concrete class (per getFormatSpecifiers).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RollingPolicyBase::getFileNamePattern
functions.description: Returns the currently configured file name pattern for the rolling policy.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RollingPolicyBase::getCreateIntermediateDirectories
functions.description: Returns whether the policy is configured to create intermediate (parent) directories when rolling files.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RollingPolicyBase::setCreateIntermediateDirectories
functions.description: Configures whether the rolling policy should create intermediate directories as needed for the output file path.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RollingPolicyBase::getPatternConverterList
functions.description: Returns the list of compiled pattern converters derived from the file name pattern. Typically populated when the pattern is parsed (e.g., during activateOptions).
requirements: Callers should ensure the file name pattern has been set and options activated so the converter list is initialized (inferred from typical OptionHandler flow).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::TimeBasedRollingPolicy::TimeBasedRollingPolicy
functions.description: Constructs a TimeBasedRollingPolicy, a rolling/triggering policy that rolls files based on time using a FileNamePattern containing a %d date token. Use setOption (or configuration) to set options and call activateOptions() before use.

If configuring programmatically, call activateOptions() after setting options and before the owning RollingFileAppender's activateOptions().

functions.description: Destructor for TimeBasedRollingPolicy. Cleans up any internal resources. No direct caller responsibilities are documented.

functions.description: Enables or disables multi-process support for coordinating state (e.g., the last rolled filename) across processes. Exact behavior is not documented here but is implied by the presence of shared-memory/mmap helpers in this class.

Should be set prior to activateOptions() for predictable effect (inferred from typical option lifecycle).

append indicates whether the new active file should be opened in append mode.

functions.signature: bool LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::TimeBasedRollingPolicy::isTriggeringEvent(LOG4CXX_NS::Appender* appender, const LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEventPtr& event, const LOG4CXX_NS::LogString& filename, size_t fileLength)

functions.signature: void LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::TimeBasedRollingPolicy::setOption(const LOG4CXX_NS::LogString& option, const LOG4CXX_NS::LogString& value)

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::TimeBasedRollingPolicy::loadLastFileName
functions.description: Loads the last filename from shared memory that may have been set by another process. Intended for multi-process coordination before deciding rollover or file naming. Detailed behavior is not documented.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::SizeBasedTriggeringPolicy::SizeBasedTriggeringPolicy

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::SizeBasedTriggeringPolicy::isTriggeringEvent
functions.signature: bool LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::SizeBasedTriggeringPolicy::isTriggeringEvent(LOG4CXX_NS::Appender* appender, const LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEventPtr& event, const LOG4CXX_NS::LogString& filename, size_t fileLength)

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::SizeBasedTriggeringPolicy::setMaxFileSize
functions.description: Sets the maximum file size in bytes used by the policy to decide when to trigger a rollover.
requirements: l is a size in bytes; it must fit in size_t.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::SizeBasedTriggeringPolicy::activateOptions
functions.description: No-op implementation of OptionHandler::activateOptions for this policy. Provided for API compliance; calling it performs no action.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::SizeBasedTriggeringPolicy::setOption

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::FixedWindowRollingPolicy::FixedWindowRollingPolicy
functions.description: Default constructor for a FixedWindowRollingPolicy. Initializes a rolling policy that renames archived log files using a fixed index window (min..max) and enforces a maximum window size of 12.
requirements: No arguments required.
Before use, callers should configure at least ActiveFileName and FileNamePattern (with an "%i" integer token) via setOption() or equivalent configuration, then call activateOptions().
Defaults (unless overridden via setOption): MinIndex=1, MaxIndex=7, ThrowIOExceptionOnForkFailure=True.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::FixedWindowRollingPolicy::~FixedWindowRollingPolicy
functions.description: Destructor for FixedWindowRollingPolicy. Releases any internal resources associated with the rolling policy instance.
requirements: Object must not be used after destruction.
No special preconditions are documented.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::FixedWindowRollingPolicy::activateOptions
functions.description: Validates and applies configured options for the rolling policy. Logs a warning if an option is invalid. Should be called after all setOption() calls and before rolling takes place.
requirements: p must be a valid, initialized LOG4CXX_NS::helpers::Pool.
Should be invoked after setting options (e.g., ActiveFileName, FileNamePattern, MinIndex, MaxIndex, ThrowIOExceptionOnForkFailure).
FileNamePattern must include an integer token "%i"; ActiveFileName is required. Invalid configurations will cause warnings.
Effective window size is capped at 12 (MAX_WINDOW_SIZE).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::FixedWindowRollingPolicy::setOption
functions.signature: void LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::FixedWindowRollingPolicy::setOption(const LOG4CXX_NS::LogString& option, const LOG4CXX_NS::LogString& value)
functions.description: Sets a configuration option for the rolling policy. Supported options include MinIndex, MaxIndex, and ThrowIOExceptionOnForkFailure, as well as properties like ActiveFileName and FileNamePattern inherited from the base policy.
requirements: option must be a recognized key. Supported keys (from this header/docs): MinIndex, MaxIndex, ThrowIOExceptionOnForkFailure. Other base-class options (e.g., ActiveFileName, FileNamePattern) may also be supported.
For MinIndex: value must represent an integer in the range 1–12 (default 1).
For MaxIndex: value must represent an integer in the range 1–12 (default 7).
For ThrowIOExceptionOnForkFailure: value must be "True" or "False" (default True).
FileNamePattern, if set, must include an integer token "%i" somewhere in the pattern.
Call activateOptions() after the last setOption() to validate/apply settings.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::FixedWindowRollingPolicy::rollover
functions.description: Performs the fixed-window rollover operation: shifts archived files within the configured index window [MinIndex..MaxIndex], deletes the oldest (max) file, renames each file up by one index, and renames the active file to MinIndex; then a new active file is created.
requirements: ActiveFileName must be set.
FileNamePattern must be set and include an "%i" integer token.
MinIndex and MaxIndex must be configured such that 1 ≤ MinIndex ≤ MaxIndex ≤ 12. The implementation may automatically reduce window size to 12.
Call activateOptions() after configuration and before calling rollover().
The underlying filesystem must permit delete/rename operations of the target files.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::FixedWindowRollingPolicy::rollover
functions.signature: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::RolloverDescriptionPtr LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::FixedWindowRollingPolicy::rollover(const LOG4CXX_NS::LogString& currentActiveFile, const bool append, LOG4CXX_NS::helpers::Pool& pool)
functions.description: Creates a RolloverDescription describing the actions to perform for a rollover of the given active file, following the fixed-window algorithm (delete max, shift indices, rename active to MinIndex, create new active). Typically called by the rolling appender when a trigger condition is met.
requirements: currentActiveFile must be the path to the current active log file.
append must be a valid boolean indicating append behavior for the new active file.
pool must be a valid, initialized LOG4CXX_NS::helpers::Pool.
ActiveFileName must be set, and FileNamePattern must include an "%i" token.
MinIndex and MaxIndex must satisfy 1 ≤ MinIndex ≤ MaxIndex ≤ 12.
Call activateOptions() after configuration and before invoking rollover().
Filesystem must allow required delete/rename operations.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::FixedWindowRollingPolicy::getMinIndex
functions.description: Returns the configured minimum index used by the fixed-window rollover algorithm.
requirements: No preconditions; callable any time after construction.
Return value is an integer in the range 1–12 (and should be ≤ MaxIndex).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::FixedWindowRollingPolicy::setMaxIndex
functions.description: Sets the maximum index for the fixed-window rollover algorithm.
requirements: newVal must be in the range 1–12; larger values are reduced to the maximum window size (12) by the implementation.
newVal should be ≥ current MinIndex.
Call activateOptions() after changing options to validate/apply settings.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::FixedWindowRollingPolicy::setMinIndex
functions.description: Sets the minimum index for the fixed-window rollover algorithm.
requirements: newVal must be in the range 1–12.
newVal should be ≤ current MaxIndex.
Call activateOptions() after changing options to validate/apply settings.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::FixedWindowRollingPolicy::initialize

functions.description: Prepares a RolloverDescription for the current active file based on the configured fixed-window policy. Typically invoked by the rolling appender framework to set up the first rollover state.
