functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::FilterBasedTriggeringPolicy::isTriggeringEvent
functions.signature: bool LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::FilterBasedTriggeringPolicy::isTriggeringEvent(LOG4CXX_NS::Appender* appender, const LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEventPtr& event, const LOG4CXX_NS::LogString& filename, size_t fileLength) override
functions.description: Evaluates the given logging event against the policy’s filter chain to determine whether a rollover should be triggered. Returns true if a rollover should occur; the RolloverPolicy will then be invoked and may still decide not to roll over. Intended to be called by the rolling appender during append processing for the active log file identified by filename and fileLength.
requirements: appender must refer to the appender invoking the check (unknown whether null is permitted).
event should reference the currently processed logging event; must be a valid LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEventPtr.
filename should be the path/name of the currently active log file associated with the appender.
fileLength should be the current size of the active file in bytes; callers should supply an accurate value for correct behavior.
Return value must be checked by the caller to decide whether to invoke rollover logic (even when true, the RolloverPolicy may still decline rollover).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::FilterBasedTriggeringPolicy::addFilter
functions.description: Appends a filter to the end of the internal filter chain used to evaluate events for triggering rollover.
requirements: newFilter should be a valid filter object (behavior for null/empty FilterPtr is not documented).
Should be called during configuration, before events are evaluated or before activateOptions (filters are activated in activateOptions).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::FilterBasedTriggeringPolicy::clearFilters
functions.description: Removes all filters from the internal filter chain, resulting in no filters being applied when evaluating events for rollover decisions.
requirements: May be called at configuration time to reset the filter chain. Effects on concurrent access are not documented.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::FilterBasedTriggeringPolicy::getFilter
functions.description: Returns a reference to the head FilterPtr of the internal filter chain used by this triggering policy.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid only as long as the policy object is alive and the filter chain is not modified (exact lifetime/ownership semantics are not documented).
Callers should avoid invalidating internal state; modifications through the returned reference affect the policy’s filter chain.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::FilterBasedTriggeringPolicy::activateOptions
functions.description: Activates all attached filters after configuration. Typically called by the configuration framework once options are set and filters are attached.
requirements: Must be called after configuration and after adding filters to ensure they are activated.
Requires a valid LOG4CXX_NS::helpers::Pool reference for any allocations performed during activation.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::FilterBasedTriggeringPolicy::setOption
functions.signature: void LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::FilterBasedTriggeringPolicy::setOption(const LOG4CXX_NS::LogString& option, const LOG4CXX_NS::LogString& value) override
functions.description: Sets a configuration option by name to a value for this policy. The header does not document specific supported options or defaults. Typically used during configuration parsing prior to activateOptions.
requirements: option must be a valid option name recognized by this policy; supported options are unknown based on the provided header.
value is the string representation for the option; expected formats/ranges are unknown based on the provided header.
Should be called before activateOptions so options take effect.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::TriggeringPolicy::~TriggeringPolicy
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the TriggeringPolicy interface. Ensures proper cleanup via a base-class pointer when deleting derived policy instances. Typical usage is to destroy a concrete TriggeringPolicy through a pointer/reference to this base type.
requirements: The object must have been constructed (fully initialized) before destruction.
Derived classes should ensure any allocated resources are released in their destructor.
Callers deleting through a base pointer must ensure the pointer actually points to a TriggeringPolicy-derived object.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::TriggeringPolicy::isTriggeringEvent
functions.signature: virtual bool LOG4CXX_NS::rolling::TriggeringPolicy::isTriggeringEvent(LOG4CXX_NS::Appender* appender, const LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEventPtr& event, const LOG4CXX_NS::LogString& filename, size_t fileLength) = 0;
functions.description: Determines whether a rollover should be triggered at the time of the given logging event. If this method returns true, the rolling subsystem may invoke the configured RolloverPolicy to perform a rollover; that policy can still decide not to proceed. Implemented by concrete TriggeringPolicy classes (e.g., size- or time-based). Typical usage: called by a rolling appender for each event or at appropriate intervals to decide if rollover criteria are met.
requirements: This is a pure virtual function; it must be implemented by a concrete subclass before use.
appender must be a valid, non-null pointer to the appender invoking the policy (the associated appender).
event must reference the current logging event being processed.
filename must be the path/name of the currently active log file.
fileLength must be the current size of the active log file in bytes and should correspond to the provided filename.
Implementations should be side-effect free beyond decision making (no requirement stated, but typical for predicate-style methods).
Return true to indicate rollover may be appropriate; false otherwise.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::DenyAllFilter::DenyAllFilter
functions.description: Default constructor for a filter that denies all logging events. Typically used by adding an instance to the end of a filter chain to switch behavior to "deny all unless instructed otherwise." No initialization parameters are required.
requirements: No arguments required.
No special initialization or state is required before constructing this object.
Constructible at any time; thread-safety of construction depends on surrounding usage (library does not specify here).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::DenyAllFilter::decide
functions.description: Evaluates a logging event against this filter and always denies it. The event parameter is ignored; the method unconditionally returns spi::Filter::DENY. Use when you need the filter chain to reject all events unless an earlier filter accepts them.
requirements: The caller must pass a spi::LoggingEventPtr (may be null; it is not dereferenced by this implementation).
The return value must be handled by the caller according to the filter chain semantics (DENY indicates the event should be rejected).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::LevelMatchFilter::LevelMatchFilter
functions.description: Constructs a LevelMatchFilter with default settings. By default, AcceptOnMatch is true and no levelToMatch is set until configured via setOption or setLevelToMatch. Typical usage is to instantiate the filter and configure options before attaching it to an appender or logger.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::LevelMatchFilter::~LevelMatchFilter
functions.description: Destroys the LevelMatchFilter instance and releases any associated resources. No special cleanup is required by callers.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::LevelMatchFilter::setOption
functions.signature: void LOG4CXX_NS::filter::LevelMatchFilter::setOption(const LogString& option, const LogString& value)
functions.description: Sets a configuration option on the filter. Supported options are LevelToMatch (the log level to match) and AcceptOnMatch (whether to accept or deny when a match occurs). Use in configuration parsing or direct programmatic setup prior to using the filter.
requirements: Option name must be either "LevelToMatch" or "AcceptOnMatch" (case sensitivity and whitespace handling are unknown).
For option "LevelToMatch", value must be one of: Trace, Debug, Info, Warn, Error, Fatal, Off, All, or a custom level formatted as "{levelName}#{registeredClassName}".
For option "AcceptOnMatch", value must be either "True" or "False".
Default for AcceptOnMatch is True if not explicitly set.
If LevelToMatch is not set, the filter will behave as NEUTRAL for all events.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::LevelMatchFilter::setLevelToMatch
functions.description: Sets the level value to compare against each event’s level when deciding. Use this to programmatically configure the level instead of setOption.
requirements: levelToMatch must specify a valid level name: Trace, Debug, Info, Warn, Error, Fatal, Off, All, or a custom level in the form "{levelName}#{registeredClassName}".
Behavior if an invalid/unknown level string is provided is unspecified (unknown).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::LevelMatchFilter::getLevelToMatch
functions.description: Returns the current level string configured for matching. If unset, this may be an empty string (exact unset representation is unknown).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::LevelMatchFilter::setAcceptOnMatch
functions.description: Sets whether a matching event should be accepted (true) or denied (false). Default is true. Configure before the filter is used.
requirements: Argument must be a boolean value.
Default behavior is AcceptOnMatch = true if not set.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::LevelMatchFilter::getAcceptOnMatch
functions.description: Returns the current AcceptOnMatch setting indicating whether matches will be accepted (true) or denied (false).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::LevelMatchFilter::decide
functions.description: Evaluates the given LoggingEvent against the configured levelToMatch and returns the filter decision. If levelToMatch is not set or does not exactly match the event’s level, returns NEUTRAL. If levels match, returns ACCEPT when AcceptOnMatch is true, otherwise returns DENY. Use during filtering stages in appenders or loggers.
requirements: Function relies on the event’s level; events are expected to carry a valid level (as is standard for LoggingEvent).
Exact matching semantics (case sensitivity, custom level resolution) follow the configured level string; details beyond the documented formats are unknown.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::LevelRangeFilter::LevelRangeFilter
functions.description: Default constructor for a LevelRange-based filter. Initializes the filter with default bounds (no minimum, no maximum) and accept-on-match behavior as described by the class defaults. Typical usage: construct, configure levelMin/levelMax and acceptOnMatch (via setOption or the specific setters), then attach to an appender or logger filter chain.
requirements: May be called any time before the filter is used in a logging pipeline.
No arguments; creates an instance in a valid, default-initialized state.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::LevelRangeFilter::~LevelRangeFilter
functions.description: Destructor for LevelRangeFilter. Cleans up any internal resources. Typically invoked automatically when the filter’s lifetime ends (e.g., when removed from an appender or going out of scope).
requirements: Do not use the object after destruction.
Ensure no concurrent use while being destroyed (thread-safety not specified).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::LevelRangeFilter::setOption
functions.signature: void LOG4CXX_NS::filter::LevelRangeFilter::setOption(const LogString& option, const LogString& value)
functions.description: Sets a configuration option by name. Supported options: LevelMin, LevelMax, AcceptOnMatch. LevelMin/LevelMax accept a level name (Trace, Debug, Info, Warn, Error, Fatal, Off, All) or a custom level in the form {levelName}#{registeredClassName}. AcceptOnMatch accepts True or False. Intended for programmatic or property-based configuration.
requirements: option must be one of: "LevelMin", "LevelMax", or "AcceptOnMatch" (other values are unspecified).
For option=="LevelMin" or "LevelMax": value must be a recognized level name (Trace, Debug, Info, Warn, Error, Fatal, Off, All) or a custom level string of the form {levelName}#{registeredClassName}.
For option=="AcceptOnMatch": value must be "True" or "False" (case-sensitivity not specified).
If an option is omitted, defaults apply: LevelMin defaults to ALL, LevelMax defaults to OFF, AcceptOnMatch defaults to True (per documentation table).
Caller should handle any errors from invalid values (error signaling mechanism not specified in the header).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::LevelRangeFilter::setLevelMin
functions.description: Sets the lower inclusive bound (levelMin) for matching. Events below this level will be denied when the range check applies. If levelMin is not defined, there is no minimum bound.
requirements: levelMin1 should refer to a valid Level instance; passing a null LevelPtr indicates “not defined” (inferred from documentation stating levelMin can be not defined).
Call before decide() is used to ensure the desired behavior is in effect.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::LevelRangeFilter::getLevelMin
functions.description: Returns the current lower inclusive bound (levelMin) for the filter, or an empty/null LevelPtr reference if not defined.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid only as long as the LevelRangeFilter object remains alive.
Do not store the reference beyond the filter’s lifetime; copy the LevelPtr if longer retention is needed.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::LevelRangeFilter::setLevelMax
functions.description: Sets the upper inclusive bound (levelMax) for matching. Events above this level will be denied when the range check applies. If levelMax is not defined, there is no maximum bound.
requirements: levelMax1 should refer to a valid Level instance; passing a null LevelPtr indicates “not defined” (inferred from documentation stating levelMax can be not defined).
Call before decide() is used to ensure the desired behavior is in effect.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::LevelRangeFilter::getLevelMax
functions.description: Returns the current upper inclusive bound (levelMax) for the filter, or an empty/null LevelPtr reference if not defined.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid only as long as the LevelRangeFilter object remains alive.
Do not store the reference beyond the filter’s lifetime; copy the LevelPtr if longer retention is needed.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::LevelRangeFilter::setAcceptOnMatch
functions.description: Sets whether matching events (within the [levelMin, levelMax] range) are accepted (ACCEPT) or passed on neutrally (NEUTRAL). When true, matching events are ACCEPT; when false, matching events are NEUTRAL.
requirements: acceptOnMatch1 is a boolean flag; choose true to ACCEPT on match, false to return NEUTRAL on match.
Call before decide() is used to ensure the desired behavior is in effect.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::LevelRangeFilter::getAcceptOnMatch
functions.description: Returns the current accept-on-match flag controlling the filter’s decision when an event level is within the configured range.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::LevelRangeFilter::decide
functions.description: Evaluates the given LoggingEvent against the configured level range. If the event’s level is outside [levelMin, levelMax] (excluding any bound that is not defined), returns DENY. If inside the range, returns ACCEPT when acceptOnMatch is true, otherwise returns NEUTRAL. If neither bound is defined, behavior reduces to acceptOnMatch for any level.
requirements: event must be a non-null spi::LoggingEventPtr referencing a valid LoggingEvent (inferred from its use).
The filter’s bounds (levelMin/levelMax) and acceptOnMatch should be set appropriately before calling decide().
Caller should be prepared to handle all three outcomes: DENY, NEUTRAL, or ACCEPT.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::LocationInfoFilter::LocationInfoFilter
functions.description: Default constructor for a filter that can enable or disable log statements based on source location (method name and/or line number) when location information is available. Typically constructed and configured by the Log4cxx framework via setOption or explicit setters.
requirements: No arguments required.
Object is initially unconfigured; callers should set options (method name, line number, operator, accept-on-match) before use if specific behavior is desired.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::LocationInfoFilter::~LocationInfoFilter
functions.description: Destructor for LocationInfoFilter. Releases any internal resources. Normally managed by the Log4cxx framework.
requirements: Do not use the object after destruction.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::LocationInfoFilter::setOption
functions.signature: void LOG4CXX_NS::filter::LocationInfoFilter::setOption(const LOG4CXX_NS::LogString& option, const LOG4CXX_NS::LogString& value)
functions.description: Sets a configuration option by name. Supported options: Method (method name to match), LineNumber (integer), Operator ("And" or default "Or" to control whether both or either of method/line must match), AcceptOnMatch (True/False; default True). Intended to be called by the Log4cxx configuration system; can also be used directly.
requirements: option must be one of: "Method", "LineNumber", "Operator", "AcceptOnMatch".
For option="LineNumber", value must represent an integer parsable by the implementation.
For option="Operator", value may be "And" to require both method and line to match; any other value implies OR semantics (default is Or).
For option="AcceptOnMatch", value should be "True" or "False" (case sensitivity not specified).
If unsupported options are provided, behavior is implementation-defined (not documented).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::LocationInfoFilter::setLineNumber
functions.description: Sets the source line number to match against when evaluating logging events’ location information.
requirements: lineNum is an int; no specific range constraints are documented.
Meaningful effect requires that events carry location information or that the filter injects it when conditions are met (see decide).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::LocationInfoFilter::setMethodName
functions.description: Sets the source method name to match against when evaluating logging events’ location information.
requirements: methodName can be any LogString; no format constraints are documented.
Meaningful effect requires that events carry method-name location information or that the filter injects it when conditions are met (see decide).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::LocationInfoFilter::setAcceptOnMatch
functions.description: Enables or disables accept-on-match behavior (default True) for the filter configuration. Note: The class-level comment for decide indicates it returns NEUTRAL; therefore the effect of this flag on the decision is unclear from this header and may be unused here.
requirements: acceptOnMatch1 is a boolean.
Default behavior if not set is True as per the options table.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::LocationInfoFilter::getAcceptOnMatch
functions.description: Returns the current accept-on-match setting (True/False).
requirements: None beyond that the object must be a valid, initialized LocationInfoFilter instance.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::LocationInfoFilter::getMustMatchAll
functions.description: Returns whether both method name and line number must match (corresponds to Operator == "And").
requirements: None beyond that the object must be a valid, initialized LocationInfoFilter instance.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::LocationInfoFilter::setMustMatchAll
functions.description: Sets whether both method name and line number must match (equivalent to setting Operator to "And"). When false, a match on either is sufficient ("Or").
requirements: mustMatchAll1 is a boolean.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::LocationInfoFilter::decide
functions.description: Evaluates the logging event against the configured location criteria. If the event does not already contain location information and the configured expression evaluates to true, the filter generates a LocationInfo (by creating an exception) and sets it on the event. According to the comment, this method always returns NEUTRAL, implying it does not accept or deny events, only possibly augments them.
requirements: event must be a valid, non-null LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEventPtr.
Location information must be available or derivable; if unavailable, the filter may do nothing.
Callers should not rely on ACCEPT/DENY; per documentation, the return value is Filter::NEUTRAL.

functions.name: log4cxx::filter::LoggerMatchFilter::LoggerMatchFilter
functions.description: Default-constructs a LoggerMatchFilter. By default, it uses loggerToMatch="root" and acceptOnMatch=true as documented. Typically used in a filter chain to accept/deny events based on the logger name.
requirements: No arguments required.
Object must be constructed before any other member function is called.
Initial defaults per docs: LoggerToMatch defaults to "root" and AcceptOnMatch defaults to true.

functions.name: log4cxx::filter::LoggerMatchFilter::~LoggerMatchFilter
functions.description: Destroys the LoggerMatchFilter instance and releases any internal resources. Intended for use when removing the filter from a logger/appender or when it goes out of scope.
requirements: The object must not be used after destruction.
If part of a filter chain owned elsewhere, ensure the owning structure does not access this filter after it is destroyed.

functions.name: log4cxx::filter::LoggerMatchFilter::setOption
functions.signature: void log4cxx::filter::LoggerMatchFilter::setOption(const log4cxx::LogString& option, const log4cxx::LogString& value) override
functions.description: Sets an option by name on the filter. Supported options are "LoggerToMatch" (any string; default "root") and "AcceptOnMatch" ("True" or "False"; default "True"). Used by configuration frameworks to programmatically configure the filter.
requirements: option must be one of: "LoggerToMatch", "AcceptOnMatch" (per documented supported options).
For option=="LoggerToMatch", value may be any string; a value of "root" matches both the root logger and a logger named "root".
For option=="AcceptOnMatch", value must be either "True" or "False" (string as documented).
Behavior for unsupported option names is unspecified in this header; callers should only pass documented options.
Case-sensitivity of option names/values is not specified; callers should use the exact forms shown in the documentation.

functions.name: log4cxx::filter::LoggerMatchFilter::setLoggerToMatch
functions.description: Sets the logger name to match against incoming events. If the event’s logger name exactly equals this string, decide() will accept or deny based on acceptOnMatch. A setting of "root" matches both the root logger and a logger literally named "root".
requirements: levelToMatch may be any string; matching is exact as documented.
A value of "root" has special handling: matches the root logger and a logger named "root".
Call before decide() to affect filtering behavior.

functions.name: log4cxx::filter::LoggerMatchFilter::getLoggerToMatch
functions.description: Returns the current logger name that this filter matches against.
requirements: None beyond the object being a valid, live instance.

functions.name: log4cxx::filter::LoggerMatchFilter::setAcceptOnMatch
functions.description: Sets whether a matching logger name should cause ACCEPT (true) or DENY (false) in decide().
requirements: Boolean argument must be provided.
Call before decide() to affect filtering behavior.

functions.name: log4cxx::filter::LoggerMatchFilter::getAcceptOnMatch
functions.description: Returns whether the filter will ACCEPT (true) or DENY (false) when the logger name matches.
requirements: None beyond the object being a valid, live instance.

functions.name: log4cxx::filter::LoggerMatchFilter::decide
functions.description: Evaluates the given LoggingEvent against the configured loggerToMatch. If loggerToMatch is not set or does not match the event’s logger, returns NEUTRAL. If it matches, returns ACCEPT when acceptOnMatch is true, otherwise returns DENY. Note: a loggerToMatch of "root" matches both the root logger and a logger named "root".
requirements: event must be a valid (non-null) spi::LoggingEventPtr.
The function does not modify event (const).
Callers should handle the returned FilterDecision according to the filter chain semantics (ACCEPT, DENY, NEUTRAL).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::StringMatchFilter::StringMatchFilter
functions.description: Default constructor for a StringMatchFilter. Initializes the filter with default options (AcceptOnMatch defaults to true; StringToMatch has no default). Typically used when constructing and configuring the filter prior to attaching it to an appender or logger.
requirements: Must be followed by configuration via setOption or the specific setters before meaningful use in decide().
Object must remain alive while used by logging framework components.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::StringMatchFilter::~StringMatchFilter
functions.description: Destructor for StringMatchFilter. Cleans up any internal resources associated with the filter instance.
requirements: Do not use the object after destruction.
Ensure no concurrent calls to decide() or setters occur during destruction (thread-safety not specified).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::StringMatchFilter::setOption
functions.signature: void LOG4CXX_NS::filter::StringMatchFilter::setOption(const LogString& option, const LogString& value);
functions.description: Sets a configuration option by name. Supported options are StringToMatch (arbitrary string) and AcceptOnMatch (True or False). Called by the configuration framework or manually by users to configure the filter’s behavior.
requirements: option must be one of: "StringToMatch" or "AcceptOnMatch" (as documented).
For option "StringToMatch", value may be any string.
For option "AcceptOnMatch", value must be either "True" or "False" (as documented; other forms are unspecified).
Call before using decide() for predictable behavior.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::StringMatchFilter::setStringToMatch
functions.description: Sets the substring to search for in incoming LoggingEvent messages. Used to configure the match criterion for this filter.
requirements: stringToMatch1 may be any string; behavior when empty implies no matches and thus NEUTRAL from decide().
Should be called before decide() to establish match criteria.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::StringMatchFilter::getStringToMatch
functions.description: Returns the currently configured match string used by the filter.
requirements: Returned reference remains valid only as long as the StringMatchFilter object remains alive.
Result is read-only (const).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::StringMatchFilter::setAcceptOnMatch
functions.description: Sets whether the filter should ACCEPT or DENY when the message contains the configured StringToMatch. If true, matching events are ACCEPTed; if false, they are DENYed.
requirements: acceptOnMatch1 must be a boolean value.
Should be set prior to invoking decide() for intended behavior.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::StringMatchFilter::getAcceptOnMatch
functions.description: Returns the current AcceptOnMatch flag that determines whether matching events are ACCEPTed or DENYed.
requirements: None beyond a valid filter instance.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::StringMatchFilter::decide
functions.description: Evaluates the given LoggingEvent. If the event message contains the configured StringToMatch, returns ACCEPT if AcceptOnMatch is true, otherwise DENY. If there is no match, returns NEUTRAL.
requirements: event must reference a valid spi::LoggingEvent (should not be null).
Behavior depends on prior configuration via setStringToMatch and setAcceptOnMatch; with no StringToMatch set, no match occurs and NEUTRAL is returned (per documentation).
Caller should handle the returned FilterDecision values (ACCEPT, DENY, NEUTRAL) according to the logging framework’s contract.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::AndFilter::AndFilter
functions.description: Default constructor for an AndFilter, which aggregates multiple child filters and combines their decisions with a logical AND. Typically used in an appender's filter chain to only accept events that match all contained filters. Initializes internal state and an empty list of child filters.
requirements: No special preconditions are specified.
Thread-safety and ownership semantics are unknown.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::AndFilter::~AndFilter
functions.description: Destructor for AndFilter. Releases any resources and contained filters managed by this filter instance.
requirements: The object must not be used after destruction.
Thread-safety and lifetime requirements relative to concurrent logging are unknown.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::AndFilter::addFilter
functions.description: Adds a child filter whose decision will be combined with others using logical AND semantics. All added filters must accept an event for the AndFilter to consider it a match.
requirements: filter should refer to a valid LOG4CXX_NS::spi::Filter instance (inferred from the API and typical usage).
Passing a null FilterPtr is unspecified/unknown.
Order of invocation relative to decide() and thread-safety are unspecified/unknown.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::AndFilter::setAcceptOnMatch
functions.description: Sets the final decision returned when all contained filters accept an event. If true, the AndFilter returns ACCEPT on full match; if false, it returns DENY on full match. When not all contained filters accept, the AndFilter returns NEUTRAL.
requirements: acceptOnMatch is a boolean; no additional constraints are specified.
Effect on in-flight decide() calls and thread-safety are unspecified/unknown.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::AndFilter::decide
functions.description: Determines the filter decision for a logging event by evaluating all contained filters. If all contained filters return Filter::ACCEPT, this returns ACCEPT when acceptOnMatch is true, or DENY when acceptOnMatch is false. If any contained filter does not return ACCEPT, this returns Filter::NEUTRAL. Intended to be called by appenders during event filtering.
requirements: event should be a non-null LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEventPtr referring to a valid logging event (inferred from API and common patterns).
No exceptions or error codes are documented; callers should handle the returned FilterDecision appropriately.
Behavior with zero contained filters is unspecified/unknown.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::MapFilter::MapFilter
functions.description: Constructs a MapFilter that matches LoggingEvents against the current thread's MDC key/value map. By default, AcceptOnMatch is true and the operator is OR (at least one configured key/value must match). Use setOption or the setters to configure behavior before calling decide.
requirements: Must be constructed before use; configure options before passing events to decide.

Not documented as thread-safe for concurrent mutation; if shared across threads, avoid modifying configuration (setOption/setKeyValue/setAcceptOnMatch/setMustMatchAll) while other threads call decide.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::MapFilter::~MapFilter
functions.description: Destroys the MapFilter and releases any associated resources or internal state.
requirements: Do not call any member functions on the MapFilter instance after destruction.
Ensure no references returned by getValue are used after the MapFilter is destroyed.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::MapFilter::setOption
functions.signature: void LOG4CXX_NS::filter::MapFilter::setOption(const LOG4CXX_NS::LogString& option, const LOG4CXX_NS::LogString& value)
functions.description: Sets a configuration option for the filter (implements spi::OptionHandler::setOption). Supported options: Operator ("And" to require all key/value pairs to match, otherwise OR logic is used), AcceptOnMatch ("True" or "False"), and arbitrary key names with their desired match value to populate the map of required MDC entries.
requirements: option must be one of: "Operator", "AcceptOnMatch", or an MDC key name to be matched.
For option "Operator", value "And" enforces all configured key/value pairs must match; any other value implies OR semantics.
For option "AcceptOnMatch", value must be "True" or "False" (string).
For arbitrary MDC key options, value is the required MDC value to match.
Call this before decide is used to evaluate events.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::MapFilter::setKeyValue
functions.signature: void LOG4CXX_NS::filter::MapFilter::setKeyValue(const LOG4CXX_NS::LogString& strKey, const LOG4CXX_NS::LogString& strValue)
functions.description: Adds or updates a single MDC key/value criterion that this filter will test against the current thread's MDC when decide is called.
requirements: strKey is treated as an MDC key; no explicit restrictions on format are documented.
Call before decide to affect filtering results.
Not documented as thread-safe; avoid calling concurrently with decide on the same instance.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::MapFilter::getValue
functions.description: Returns the configured value associated with the given MDC key in this filter's internal key/value criteria. If the key was not configured, the exact return (e.g., empty string vs. sentinel) is not documented.
requirements: strKey is the configuration key previously provided via setOption or setKeyValue.

The returned reference remains valid only as long as the MapFilter object exists and its configuration is not modified in a way that would invalidate internal storage (exact guarantees not documented).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::MapFilter::setAcceptOnMatch
functions.description: Sets whether events that match the configured MDC criteria should be accepted (true) or denied (false) by decide. If no criteria match, decide will return NEUTRAL.
requirements: Pass true to accept on match, false to deny on match.
Call before decide to affect behavior.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::MapFilter::getAcceptOnMatch

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::MapFilter::getMustMatchAll
functions.description: Returns whether all configured key/value pairs must match the MDC (AND semantics) rather than only one (OR semantics).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::MapFilter::setMustMatchAll
functions.description: Sets whether all configured key/value pairs must match (true for AND semantics) or at least one must match (false for OR semantics). Equivalent to setting option "Operator" to "And" when true, or to OR when false.
requirements: Call before decide to affect evaluation semantics.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::MapFilter::decide
functions.description: Evaluates the given event against the current thread's MDC and the filter's configured key/value criteria. Returns NEUTRAL if there is no string match. If criteria match, returns ACCEPT or DENY depending on AcceptOnMatch; exact enum type is that of spi::Filter's FilterDecision.
requirements: event should be a valid, non-null LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEventPtr.
Relies on the current thread's MDC contents; callers expecting specific behavior must ensure proper MDC population prior to calling decide.
If no configured key/value criteria are present or no matches are found, the function returns NEUTRAL as documented.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::PropertyFilter::PropertyFilter
functions.description: Constructs a PropertyFilter, a log4cxx filter that augments logging events with additional properties. Use this to create the filter instance before configuring its property list via setProperties and attaching it to an appender or logger’s filter chain.
requirements: Must be followed by a call to setProperties(...) to have any effect on events (otherwise no properties are added).
Should be added to a logger/appender filter chain according to log4cxx usage patterns (not enforced by this API).

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::PropertyFilter::~PropertyFilter
functions.description: Destroys the PropertyFilter and releases any internal resources associated with stored properties. Typically invoked automatically when the filter object goes out of scope or is removed from the filter chain.
requirements: Filter instance must not be used after destruction.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::PropertyFilter::setProperties
functions.description: Configures the filter’s properties that will be added to each processed logging event. The input string is parsed into name/value pairs and stored; properties are only added to an event if that property is not already present on the event. Expected format: comma-delimited pairs with each pair as name=value (e.g., "somename=somevalue,another=anothervalue").
requirements: props must use comma-delimited pairs with each pair using an equals sign to delimit name and value (e.g., name=value,name2=value2).
Property names and values are interpreted as LogString; values may contain spaces as shown in the example.
If a property already exists on a logging event, this filter will not override it (behavior by design).
Call setProperties before events are processed to ensure properties are applied to those events.
Thread-safety of concurrent calls is unspecified; avoid concurrent modification from multiple threads unless guaranteed by surrounding framework.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::filter::PropertyFilter::decide
functions.description: Processes a logging event by adding the configured properties to the event if they are not already present, then returns a FilterDecision to control further processing in the filter chain. Intended to be called by the logging framework for each event passing through this filter.
requirements: event must be a valid (non-null) LOG4CXX_NS::spi::LoggingEventPtr.
The filter may modify the event by adding properties; callers should pass an event that can be safely mutated by filters.
Return value semantics (ACCEPT/NEUTRAL/DENY) are determined by the log4cxx FilterDecision contract; this header does not specify which decision is returned in each case.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::FMTLayout::FMTLayout
functions.description: Default-constructs an FMTLayout, a log4cxx Layout that formats events using {fmt}-style placeholders. Use when you plan to set the conversion pattern later via setConversionPattern or setOption.

functions.description: Constructs an FMTLayout with an initial {fmt}-style conversion pattern. The pattern can include the documented tokens (e.g., {logger}, {level}, {message}, {newline}, MDC keys mdc1..mdc6).

requirements: If using MDC placeholders (mdc1..mdc6), the corresponding MDC keys must be specified in the configuration for the layout (maximum of 6 keys).

functions.signature: inline bool operator&(HexdumpFlags a, HexdumpFlags b)
functions.description: Bitwise-intersection test for HexdumpFlags. Returns true if a and b share any common flag bit; otherwise false. Use to check whether a combined flags value includes a specific flag (e.g., if (flags & HexdumpFlags::AddStartingNewline) { ... }). Note: unlike typical operator& on enums, this overload returns a boolean rather than a HexdumpFlags value.
requirements: Parameters a and b must each be valid HexdumpFlags values.
The function does not modify state and has no side effects; it is safe to call repeatedly.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::operator|
functions.signature: inline HexdumpFlags operator|(HexdumpFlags a, HexdumpFlags b)
functions.description: Bitwise-union for HexdumpFlags. Produces a combined HexdumpFlags value containing all bits set in either a or b. Use to compose multiple formatting flags (e.g., HexdumpFlags::AddStartingNewline | HexdumpFlags::AddEndingNewline).
requirements: Parameters a and b must each be valid HexdumpFlags values.
The function does not modify state and has no side effects; it is safe to call repeatedly.

functions.name: LOG4CXX_NS::hexdump
functions.signature: LOG4CXX_EXPORT LogString hexdump(const void* bytes, uint32_t len, HexdumpFlags flags = HexdumpFlags::None)
functions.description: Formats the given byte buffer as a human-readable hexadecimal dump and returns the result as a LogString. The output resembles traditional hexdump format and may include leading/trailing newlines depending on flags. Typical use: pass a pointer to the data, its length, and optional flags such as AddStartingNewline or AddEndingNewline to control newline insertion.
requirements: bytes must point to a readable memory region of at least len bytes; if len == 0, bytes may be null.
len specifies the number of bytes to dump and must fit in uint32_t (unsigned).
flags is a combination of HexdumpFlags values; valid values include None, AddStartingNewline, AddEndingNewline, and their union AddNewline.
The function reads but does not take ownership of the memory pointed to by bytes; the buffer must remain valid for the duration of the call.
Callers should handle the returned LogString as a regular value; no special cleanup beyond normal LogString handling is required.

A filesystem path string derived from a fuzz-provided filename that points to an actual file containing random data. Used where APIs expect configuration file paths or filenames. The content of the file may be arbitrary; the path itself can include typical filename characters and directory separators.

generators.generator:
import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

def _rand_bool(r: random.Random, p: float = 0.5) -> bool:
    return r.random() < p

def _choose(r: random.Random, seq):
    return seq[r.randrange(len(seq))]

def _rand_filename(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate a plausible configuration filename with common extensions
    bases = [
        "log4cxx", "log4j", "logging", "config", "app", "server", "client",
    ]
    stems = [
        _choose(r, bases),
        _choose(r, bases) + "-" + str(r.randrange(1000)),
        _choose(r, bases) + "_" + _choose(r, ["dev","test","prod","local"]) ,
    ]
    exts = [".xml", ".properties", ".conf", ".cfg"]
    stem = _choose(r, stems)
    ext = _choose(r, exts)
    return stem + ext

def _rand_dir_components(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Create 0-3 random directory components
    comps = []
    n = r.randrange(0, 4)
    alpha = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_"
    for _ in range(n):
        l = r.randrange(1, 8)
        comps.append(''.join(r.choice(alpha) for _ in range(l)))
    return comps

def _maybe_env_placeholder(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Produce ${VAR} placeholders sometimes to exercise expansion logic
    vars_ok = [
        "PROGRAM_FILE_PATH.PARENT_PATH",
        "PROGRAM_FILE_PATH.STEM",
        "HOME",
        "TMPDIR",
        "NON_EXISTENT_ENV",
    ]
    if _rand_bool(r, 0.4):
        return "${" + _choose(r, vars_ok) + "}"
    return ""

def _build_existing_temp_path(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Point to an actually existing file inside current working directory or temp
    # We cannot perform I/O, so just return plausible temp-like paths.
    tmpdirs = ["/tmp", "/var/tmp", "tmp", "."]
    base = _rand_filename(r)
    return os.path.join(_choose(r, tmpdirs), base)

def _candidate_paths(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    paths = []
    # 1) Current directory straightforward file
    paths.append(os.path.join(".", _rand_filename(r)))
    # 2) With random subdirectories
    comps = _rand_dir_components(r)
    paths.append(os.path.join(*(comps + [_rand_filename(r)]) ) if comps else _rand_filename(r))
    # 3) Absolute-like temp path
    paths.append(_build_existing_temp_path(r))
    # 4) Include env placeholder prefix sometimes
    ph = _maybe_env_placeholder(r)
    if ph:
        paths.append(os.path.join(ph, _rand_filename(r)))
    # 5) Common defaults
    paths.append("log4cxx.xml")
    paths.append("log4cxx.properties")
    return paths

def _dedup_keep_order(seq: List[str]) -> List[str]:
    seen = set()
    out = []
    for s in seq:
        if s not in seen and s:
            seen.add(s)
            out.append(s)
    return out

def _encode_concat(items: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Encode multiple strings into a single buffer separated by nulls
    blob = "\0".join(items)
    data = blob.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a rich set of candidate path strings for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME consumers
    paths = _candidate_paths(r)

    # Build some FUZZ_PARAM_STR candidates: level names, boolean words, options, JSON/XML snippets
    levels = ["Trace","Debug","Info","Warn","Error","Fatal","Off","All"]
    bools = ["True","False","true","false"]
    # Simple file patterns and options relevant to rolling policies and layouts
    options = [
        "Threshold=Debug",
        "Encoding=UTF-8",
        "ImmediateFlush=True",
        "PrettyPrint=True",
        "LocationInfo=True",
        "BufferSize=128",
        "Blocking=False",
        "MaxFileSize=10MB",
        "MaxBackupIndex=3",
        "FileDatePattern=yyyy-MM-dd_HH",
        "Title=Log4cxx Log Messages",
    ]
    # Filenames for DefaultConfigurator::configureFromFile
    names = ["log4cxx.xml","log4cxx.properties", _rand_filename(r)]

    # Mix in placeholders for environment expansion
    placeholders = [
        _maybe_env_placeholder(r) + "/" + _rand_filename(r)
        if _rand_bool(r, 0.5) else _rand_filename(r)
        for _ in range(2)
    ]

    # Compose the ordered list: alternate filename-like and misc strings
    items: List[str] = []
    items.extend(_dedup_keep_order(paths))
    items.extend(_dedup_keep_order(names))
    items.extend(_dedup_keep_order(levels))
    items.extend(_dedup_keep_order(bools))
    items.extend(_dedup_keep_order(options))
    items.extend(_dedup_keep_order(placeholders))

    # Ensure at least one candidate that looks like an absolute Windows path, one Unix
    drive_letter = chr(ord('C') + r.randrange(0, 3))  # C, D, or E
    win_drive = f"{drive_letter}:\\\\" + _rand_filename(r)
    unix_abs = "/etc/" + _rand_filename(r)
    items.append(win_drive)
    items.append(unix_abs)

    # Return as a single bytes blob
    return _encode_concat(items)
